books.why: A father and son walk through a burned-out America in spare, haunting prose; readers call it devastating and unforgettable.
A man lives alone in an endless house of statues and tides, and slowly uncovers its secret; short, strange and beautifully written.
A lone astronaut wakes up with amnesia on a mission to save Earth; science-driven, funny and impossible to put down.
A plague wipes out most of humanity and survivors gather around good or evil figures; a huge, gripping apocalyptic saga.
Two California families echo the Cain and Abel story across generations; readers praise its big themes about good, evil and choice.
A group of classics students at an elite college drift into murder; immersive, twisty and addictive for fans of dark academia.
Four friends in New York, one carrying terrible trauma; a devastating, long read readers say they cried through, with heavy content warnings.
The quiet life of an ordinary university professor, told with simple, precise prose that moves readers more than they expect.
A young bride is haunted by her husband's dead first wife at his grand estate; gothic, gripping and famous for its opening lines.
David Copperfield retold in Appalachia, following a poor orphan through foster care and addiction; readers call it powerful and heartbreaking.
Students at a strange boarding school slowly learn what their lives are for; quiet, sad and impossible to forget.
A teenage runaway joins a band of scalp hunters in the 1850s borderlands; brutal, poetic and widely called a masterpiece.
The author grows up in a survivalist family with no schooling and ends up at Cambridge; readers find it gripping and devastating.
A short first-hand account of a teenager's time in Nazi concentration camps; readers call it essential and crushing.
A young woman survives a collapsing California and founds a new belief system; chillingly relevant dystopia that readers rate highly.
Two retired Texas Rangers drive cattle to Montana; a sprawling, character-rich western often named among the best American novels.
Jesuit missionaries make first contact with aliens and one man returns broken; readers say it is moving and haunting.
Huckleberry Finn retold from the point of view of Jim, the enslaved man; readers praise its wit, voice and power.
A boy survives a bombing and keeps a stolen painting that shapes his life; long, absorbing and well liked by many readers.
An unreliable narrator tells his own disturbing story in dazzling prose; admired for the writing, though some find it hard going.
A young nurse goes to Vietnam and struggles to come home; readers find it moving and easy to read.
A torturer exiled from his guild travels a far-future Earth in a puzzling, richly written tale; hard, but readers call it a masterpiece.
A scientist creates life and then rejects it; the founding science fiction novel, still praised for its moral questions.
A wrongly imprisoned sailor escapes and plots elaborate revenge; a long but thrilling classic that readers say flies by.
A physicist is kidnapped into a world where his life went differently; a quick, fun sci-fi thriller.
A crew meets an alien that may be smarter than they are without being conscious; hard sci-fi that readers find brilliant and chilling.
An envoy visits a planet whose people have no fixed gender; readers value its ideas and humane storytelling.
A house is bigger inside than out, told through footnotes and odd layouts; hard to put down and hard to forget.
One day in Dublin told in shifting experimental styles; very demanding, but readers enjoy it as funny and rewarding.
The witch from the Odyssey tells her own story; lyrical and absorbing myth retelling that readers love.
A lonely writing student is drawn into a clique of women with a bizarre ritual; weird, funny and unsettling.
A noble family fights for control of a desert planet and its spice; the benchmark for epic science fiction.
An American missionary family goes to the Congo and falls apart, told by wife and daughters; readers find it well written and powerful.
Seven pilgrims tell their stories on the way to a deadly shrine; a Canterbury Tales in space that readers rank among the best.
Four strangers share a flat in 1970s India as politics crush their hopes; readers say it hurts and stays with them for weeks.
Rival builders, nobles and monks struggle over a cathedral in medieval England; a long, gripping page-turner.
An expedition enters a strange, shifting zone where nature behaves wrongly; short, eerie and often recommended for fans of weird fiction.
A man with a learning disability becomes a genius through an experiment; told in diary form, it stays with readers for years.
Two sisters take different paths in occupied France in World War II; readers say it left them sobbing.
Humanity's last ship meets a world where spiders evolve intelligence; readers rave about its big ideas and inventive aliens.
Aliens turn Earth into a deadly game show and a man and his cat fight for survival; darkly funny and addictive.
The comedian's childhood in apartheid South Africa as a mixed-race child; readers laugh and cry in equal measure.
A modern Black woman is pulled back in time to a slave plantation; gripping, painful and often called her best book.
A carnival family breeds its own freak-show children; grotesque, inventive and wildly strange for readers who like shocking fiction.
After a flu ends civilization, a travelling theatre troupe keeps art alive; beautifully written and a favourite for quiet apocalypse stories.
The true story of Shackleton's ship trapped in Antarctic ice and his crew's survival; readers find it gripping and inspiring.
Monks living apart from the world are drawn into a crisis that changes it; dense and slow to start but loved for its ideas.
A woman gets to try lives she might have lived; comforting and quick to read, though a few readers found it shallow.
Four generations of a Korean family in Japan face prejudice and hardship; readers call it raw, real and moving.
The author's first-hand account of the deadly 1996 Everest disaster; readers say they could not stop reading.
A young woman slides into depression in 1950s New York; readers relate strongly and say it stays with them.
Two Ghanaian half-sisters and their descendants across 300 years; each chapter follows one generation, and readers find it powerful.
An English butler looks back on a life of duty and missed chances; subtle and quietly devastating.
An English pilot is stranded in feudal Japan and caught in a power struggle; a long, immersive adventure.
A hobbit sets out to destroy a ring of power; the founding epic of modern fantasy that readers return to again and again.
A sudden epidemic of blindness breaks down society; unusual punctuation-free prose and a harrowing story readers praise.
An astronaut stranded on Mars science his way to survival; funny, clever and a quick read.
A farming family flees the Dust Bowl for California; a powerful picture of poverty and resilience.
Abercrombie's demon-summoning fantasy comedy with bloody action; readers enjoy it so far and plan to read more of his work.
A huge, footnoted novel about addiction, tennis and entertainment; very demanding but readers say it rewards the effort.
Nine people are drawn together by trees and the fight to save forests; ambitious, moving and eye-opening.
A soldier becomes unstuck in time after surviving the Dresden bombing; short, funny and sad antiwar classic.
A study of marriages, ambition and reform in a provincial English town; long and rich, often called the greatest English novel.
A reconstruction of the 1959 murder of a Kansas family and the killers' fate; gripping true crime that reads like a novel.
The missing years of Jesus told by his best friend Biff; irreverent, hilarious and re-read yearly by fans.
A middle-aged artist upends her life on a trip that stops in a motel; funny, odd and hard to predict.
A girl steals books in Nazi Germany while Death narrates; readers love its voice and find it moving.
Rabbits flee their doomed warren and search for a new home; much more gripping and moving than it sounds.
The moon explodes and humanity races to survive in space; technical and long, but readers like its big ideas.
A psychiatrist describes surviving Nazi camps and what kept people going; short, humane and widely recommended for finding meaning in suffering.
A miner on Mars infiltrates the ruling caste to overthrow it; fast and violent, popular with fans of The Hunger Games and epic fantasy.
Backman's novel about friendship and a painting that connects four teenagers; fans who read it praise its warmth and quotable lines.

books.t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
books.why: An ordinary man is whisked off Earth moments before it is demolished; absurd, quotable comic science fiction readers love from childhood.
Two young magicians are bound in a competition inside a mysterious travelling circus; dreamy and romantic, loved for its imagery.
Captain Ahab hunts the white whale; long and digressive but readers find it funny and sublime.
A gifted orphan grows into a legendary wizard, telling his own story; lyrical and absorbing, a fan favourite.
A monk investigates murders in a medieval abbey; a learned detective story that readers find rewarding.
Seven generations of a family in a Colombian village, full of magic and fate; the classic of magical realism.
A boy finds a forgotten book in a Barcelona library of lost books and uncovers its author's mystery; gothic and bookish.
Centuries of people who live in one New England house and the woods around it; beautifully written and varied.
A poor student commits murder and is consumed by guilt; psychological and intense, it leaves readers in a deep state.
Twins in Kerala grow up under the weight of a family tragedy; fascinating and poetic, though not an easy read.
A poem and a madly unreliable commentary on it; a tricky, brilliant puzzle for readers who like playing with form.
The author grows up with brilliant but irresponsible parents who drag the family through poverty; compelling and easy to read.
Survivors of nuclear war fight over what remains of America and its soul; a huge post-apocalyptic story recommended after The Stand.
Warriors, scholars and slaves are drawn into an ancient war on a storm-swept world; Sanderson's huge opening to a vast series.
A man with a perfect sense of smell turns to murder to create the ultimate scent; strange, vivid and haunting.
People who can control the earth live in an apocalypse-prone world; inventive and gripping, a Hugo winner.
A washed-up hacker is hired for one last job in cyberspace; the novel that invented cyberpunk, dense but influential.
A historian time-travels to medieval England just as the plague hits; readers say it will break your heart.
Four people spend a summer in a haunted mansion with a fragile guest; a masterclass in subtle, creeping dread.
A man wakes up as a giant insect and his family turns away; very short, strange and widely read.
A future society engineered for happiness and control; a classic dystopia readers still find relevant.
The former child actress writes frankly about her controlling mother and her own illness; readers find it raw and darkly funny.

pl.t: Cieszę się, że moja mama umarła

books.why: A sprawling, bizarre novel set around V-2 rockets in World War II; famous as one of the hardest books to read.
Told through letters and diaries, a band of friends hunts the vampire count; surprisingly a page turner.
A young man in ancient India searches for spiritual understanding; short and lyrical, loved by many and a little preachy to some.
A group of people raised by a godlike figure are drawn into a struggle for his library; violent, strange and darkly funny.
A girl in Alabama watches her lawyer father defend a Black man; a warm, moving classic about justice.
An orphan enters an elite Roman-style academy where the powerful drain others' will; readers call it a gripping start to a series.
A troubled young woman recounts her difficult life with humour and pain; a popular emotional read.
Two ships are trapped in Arctic ice in 1845 and something hunts the crew; fiction based on a true expedition that readers cannot put down.
An obsessive love between Heathcliff and Cathy destroys two families on the Yorkshire moors; stormy and passionate.
A botanist and Potawatomi writer joins plant science with indigenous wisdom; readers love it, especially as an audiobook.
A comfort-loving hobbit is swept into a quest with dwarves to win back treasure from a dragon; a warm, easy adventure.

pl.t: Hobbit, czyli tam i z powrotem

books.why: A man dies at 43 and wakes up as his 18-year-old self, again and again; an emotional time-loop story.

books.t: The Devil in the White City
books.why: The 1893 Chicago World's Fair is told alongside a serial killer working nearby; narrative history that reads like a thriller.
A family seeks a new start in the Alaskan wilderness, but the father unravels; readers find it gripping and emotional.
In a theocratic America women are reduced to childbearing; chilling, widely recommended dystopia.
A young teacher on a Greek island is drawn into an elaborate psychological game; readers call it a crazy, gripping mystery.
A man on a walk in the woods enters a surreal world of monsters and puzzles; quick and wildly inventive.
A kind prince returns to Russian society and everything around him turns tragic; some readers find it funny; long and demanding.
A love story set among women astronauts in the early shuttle era; popular and easy to read.
A priest's journals from the 1910s describe a vampire in Montana and the Blackfeet nation; an excellent, unsettling horror novel.
A child's false accusation wrecks lives, and she spends her life atoning; admired for its ending, though a few readers find it slow.
A lone survivor recalls the genetic engineering world that ended humanity; sharp dystopia that starts the MaddAddam trilogy.
A widow befriends a clever aquarium octopus who knows a secret; a heartwarming, easy read.
A writer searches for the inventor of the atom bomb and finds a made-up religion; short, dark and funny.
A Black girl in 1940s Ohio longs for blue eyes; short and painful, often recommended for its beautiful prose.
The story of a woman taken during the Northern Ireland Troubles and the people behind her murder; gripping and surprising narrative history.
A memory-altering disease and a time device unravel reality; a fast thriller that suckers readers in.
A writer finishing another author's series finds a disturbing manuscript; an addictive, trashy thriller that kept readers up.
A street thief joins a crew to overthrow an immortal ruler using metal-based magic; inventive and fast, with a great twist.
Two friends build video games across decades; warm and moving story about creativity and friendship.
A failed bank robbery turns into a hostage situation at an apartment viewing; comic and warm.
Three generations of a Kerala family linked by a curse and by medicine; long, rich and beautifully written.
A security robot hacks its own controls and just wants to watch shows; short, charming and quick to read.
The love story of Achilles and Patroclus at Troy, told by Patroclus; readers find it beautiful and heartbreaking.
A writer is held captive by his number one fan; a tight, scary thriller recommended to anyone starting with King.
A struggling writer takes a winter caretaker job at an isolated hotel; the novel is scarier than the film.
A recovering addict and poet searches for meaning in death; readers rate it highly as a recent standout.
A pizza-delivering hacker fights a virus in the metaverse; funny, fast-moving cyberpunk.
A boy discovers the secret behind his perfectly controlled community; a short school favourite that adults say they would re-read.
After her mother's death and her marriage collapse, the author hikes the Pacific Crest Trail; moving and beautifully written.
An American in Paris struggles with desire and shame; short and intense, readers say it blew them away.
A man whose dreams change reality has a therapist who wants to use them; a short, odd, thoughtful book.
A scientist unleashes a monster in the strange city of New Crobuzon; dense, inventive new weird fantasy.
Teenage boys must keep walking in a deadly contest; short, relentless and bleak, and one reader said it hit them hard.
Shakespeare's wife and the death of their son, told in lyrical prose; readers say it made them cry.
A man who abandoned his family lives among drifters on the Tennessee river; dense, bleak and darkly funny McCarthy.
A girl travels between worlds in a fight against a powerful church; a children's trilogy that adults love.
The decline of a Southern family told through four voices, one of them mentally disabled; famously hard but admired.
A girl grows up in Ohio in a troubled Cherokee family and learns through stories; readers say they sobbed through the ending.
Space colonists live as Hindu gods on a distant planet, and one rebels; mythic, stylish and often listed among the best.
An orphan becomes a governess and falls for her mysterious employer; romantic, gothic and recommended as an accessible classic.
A solar-powered robot companion watches over a sick girl; quietly moving and hard to put down.
A woman stops speaking after killing her husband and a therapist tries to understand why; a quick thriller with a twist.
A former starship AI in a single human body seeks revenge; clever space opera that sticks to its sequels.
A child disappears from a summer camp, decades after her brother vanished; a twisty mystery that readers are enjoying.
A government experiment turns people into vampires and the survivors face an apocalyptic world; long and compelling.
A retired woman keeps up her life through letters; readers say they loved it so much they re-read it.
A boy is sent to a brutal 1950s Florida reform school haunted by the dead; a powerful horror novel rooted in history.

books.t: The House in the Cerulean Sea
books.why: A caseworker inspects an orphanage of magical children and finds a home; warm, gentle and uplifting.
A real account of an Ebola-like virus outbreak near Washington; terrifying and gripping.
Two magicians return English magic in the Napoleonic era; long, dry-witted alternate history that readers get absorbed in.
A five-year-old narrator lives in one room with his mother; a disturbing but compelling and moving story.
Immigrant workers in Chicago's meatpacking industry face hardship; relentlessly bleak and an important muckraking novel.
A boy survives alone in the Canadian wilderness after a plane crash; a quick, easy adventure that kids and adults remember.
A Black man moves through America feeling unseen; powerful, demanding and often described as a missed classic.
Six nested stories in different eras and styles echo each other; ambitious and frequently named a favourite.
A mercenary's two timelines run in opposite directions toward a revelation; many Banks fans name it his best.
A teenage boy's cruel rituals on a remote Scottish island hide a shocking secret; short and truly horrifying.
Ghosts crowd a graveyard after Lincoln's son dies; experimental, voiced chorus that moves many readers.
Four versions of a 1920s financier's story reveal different truths; readers find it amazing and easy to enjoy.
A gay man's life in Ireland from birth across seven decades; a sweeping book that readers love.
A Greek-American family saga narrated by an intersex person; multigenerational and warmly told.

books.t: The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue
books.why: A woman makes a deal to live forever but be forgotten; romantic and lyrical, liked by many readers.

pl.t: The Invisible Life of Addie La Rue

books.why: The richest man on Earth is pulled into a cosmic joke of a plan; a darkly funny early Vonnegut.
A man in America tries to atone for a childhood betrayal in Afghanistan; readers say it lives up to the hype.
A knight and a girl cross plague-ridden France in the 1300s as angels and demons clash; readers are engrossed.
A Dublin mother copes as Ireland slides into authoritarianism; relentless unpunctuated prose that readers call gripping.
Two Irish teens drift together and apart for years; spare, intense, and one reader admitted to re-reading at once.
An ex-convict tries to live a good life in 19th-century France; a huge, powerful and humane classic.
A family lives on a remote island that is near the Antarctic, with a mystery washed ashore; readers love it.
A gifted boy is trained at a space military school; a classic page-turner that readers recommend for military sci-fi.
A young man visits a sanatorium and stays for seven years; slow, philosophical and rewarding.
A boy in 1960s Alabama sees a murder and grows up with mystery and magic; a nostalgic coming-of-age favourite.

books.t: All the Light We Cannot See
books.why: A blind French girl and a German boy meet in the war; short chapters and lyrical prose make it a popular pick.
A young necromancer enters the Old Kingdom to save her father; an excellent dark fantasy aimed at teens and adults.
The woman once known as Emily Doe tells her own story after a sexual assault trial; powerful and painful.
Scientists orbit a planet that seems to read their minds; Lem's cerebral first-contact classic.
A young woman follows her father's trail across Europe in search of Dracula; slow-burning gothic mystery.

books.t: The Old Man and the Sea
books.why: An aged fisherman battles a huge marlin for days; short and simple, readers say it is deep.
Linked stories across centuries and a lost ancient book; warm and ambitious like his earlier hit.
A Black woman in Florida seeks love and her own voice; lyrical and pretty widely recommended.
Five families live through the Napoleonic wars in Russia; a huge book readers say becomes absorbing.
Codebreakers in World War II and hackers today pursue a hidden treasure; long, geeky and funny, with a beloved character.
A teacher abuses her students and narrates her own predation; very disturbing yet a page turner according to readers.
Farm animals overthrow their master and a new tyranny arises; a short allegory still read widely.

books.t: The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet
books.why: A mixed-species crew travels on a tunnelling ship; warm, character-driven space adventure.
A bomber pilot tries to escape the army's absurd rules; a funny, memorable war satire.
A detective and her assistant investigate a murder in a world with giant monsters; blends mystery and fantasy well.
A substitute teacher inherits his uncle's supervillain empire; a short and breezy comic romp.
An amnesiac wanders a ruined American city; long and strange, loved by experimental sci-fi fans.

books.t: To Say Nothing of the Dog
books.why: Time-travelling historians are sent to Victorian England to find a missing object; comic and charming.
A swordswoman and a necromancer enter a haunted space house; gothic and joking, and readers keep going to the sequels.
Friends hit the road across 1950s America; changed some readers' lives and bored others.
On an island things disappear and people forget them; quiet dystopia that people recommend.
A unicorn leaves her forest to find others like her; a lyrical, bittersweet fairy tale.
A graduate student finds a book that leads to an underground library; pretty, dreamy and loved.
A mathematician predicts the fall of a galactic empire and plans to save knowledge; a classic of ideas.
A steamboat captain travels upriver in the Congo toward the sinister Kurtz; short and dense, widely read.
A time-travelling investigator hunts a killer in a future that is ending; a gripping hybrid of thriller and sci-fi.
A coal merchant in 1985 Ireland finds a secret at a convent; a very short, quietly powerful novel.
Linked lives across centuries are connected by a strange glitch in time; a short and elegant favourite.
Writers at a retreat tell grotesque stories while isolated; shocking, fun and awful in readers' words.
Vampires take over a small Maine town; readers call it an absolute classic of horror.
The intense friendship of two girls growing up in postwar Naples; the first Neapolitan novel and a widely praised read.
A midwife investigates a death in 1789 Maine, based on a real diary; readers named it a top read.
A plague turns people into zombie-like routines while an office worker keeps going; funny and sad, called brilliant.
People in Australia wait calmly for radiation from nuclear war to arrive; a quiet and moving apocalypse story.
A pilot and his dog survive after a pandemic; lyrical post-apocalypse that readers recommend.
A ship crew uncovers a plot that may start a war across the solar system; realistic, gripping space opera.
Odysseus struggles for ten years to get home; the foundation of adventure storytelling, readers value modern translations.
A boy is sent to dig holes at a desert camp and learns its secret; clever and fast, loved since childhood.
A Chinese peasant farmer's rise and the ups and downs of his family across years; a classic family saga.
Humans on an alien world depend on a language in which one cannot lie; one reader's best ever.
A boy and a woman journey through a mythic empire; poetic and moving, with unusual storytelling.
A soldier maimed in World War I is trapped in his own mind; short and harrowing antiwar book.
Digital citizens and robots spread across the galaxy to avoid a cosmic threat; hard sci-fi with intense ideas.
A wealthy 1980s banker narrates his casual murders; very graphic and satirical, giving readers nightmares.
A teenager inherits a secret portal to another world in his neighbour's shed; readers say they did not want it to end.
A fugitive hides in Bombay and falls in with the underworld; a long, immersive tale based on the author's life.
Peaceful alien overlords arrive and change humanity's future; short and thought-provoking classic.
Two Black teens suffer in a brutal Florida reform school; spare and devastating with not a word wasted.
Two young men must find a dozen eggs during the Siege of Leningrad; fast, funny and heartfelt.
A neglected girl is sent to live with relatives in rural Ireland; a short, quietly moving story.
A tradwife influencer wakes up in the past; recommended by readers eager for it, though few have finished it.
American life from the Cold War onward, built around a baseball; astonishing, ambitious and demanding.
A student finds a secret magic college that is not as good as the Narnia of his dreams; darker and sharper.
Reality begins to decay around a team of psychic-detecting agents; short, weird and typically Dick.
A woman fears her daughter has something wrong with her; a disturbing psychological thriller about motherhood.
A medieval village suffers famine and cruelty; terrifying and grotesque and loved by the reader.
A hockey town splits after a crime; readers say it is the Backman they will always name first.
Cloned dinosaurs run wild on a theme-park island; a fast techno-thriller that beats the film.
Linked stories about soldiers in the Vietnam War, what they carry and what they tell; widely taught and often reread.
A scientist receives a message from space and must decide what it means; readers sit stunned after finishing it.
Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy fight pride on the way to love; readers return decades later and still enjoy it.
A boy crosses into Mexico several times, with a wolf and a loss; sublime, spare and demanding in his pace.
A vengeful man with strange powers pursues rich enemies across the solar system; a classic that drags readers along.
A soldier fights an interstellar war while time dilation leaves him lost at home; short and reality-minded military sci-fi.
A family holiday on a Scottish island unfolds through shifting inner thoughts; lyrical but demanding.
A princess who dislikes being a princess goes to live with dragons; funny, clever children's fantasy fondly remembered.
Two migrant workers dream of a farm of their own; very short and heartbreaking.
A small town holds its yearly ritual; a very short, shocking story whose tropes started here.
An Olympic runner survives a plane crash, the sea and a prison camp in World War II; a testament to the will to live.
A poor Southern family carries their mother's coffin to burial through a series of voices; short but difficult.
A mother in newly independent India searches for a husband for her daughter; a huge, absorbing family novel.

books.t: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
books.why: An old film star tells a young journalist about her many marriages; easy and addictive, recommended widely.
Poirot investigates a village murder with a famous twist; readers love it and its ending.
Thomas Cromwell rises in Henry VIII's court; rich and intense, though the style is demanding.
A girl hires a rough marshal to find her father's killer; sharp-voiced, funny western.

books.t: All the Colors of the Dark
books.why: A long mystery about a missing girl in 1970s Missouri; readers are drawn in by its characters.
A historian cursed to relive a king's life shapes history across time; could not be put down according to readers.
A boy's rise from a hard childhood to novelist; warm, long Dickens with many memorable characters.
Boy scouts on a remote island face a horrifying infection; gruesome and fast, a repeat read for horror fans.
Clones of one person travel the galaxy and meet a threat; vast space opera readers return to.
A Texas family struggles in the Dust Bowl, especially the second half; emotional and popular.
A boy facing his mother's illness is visited by a tree monster; short and moving, best in the illustrated edition.
A woman crashes a wedding at a hotel while at a low point; light, funny and heartfelt.
A frail woman enters a war college where cadets bond with dragons; polarising but a binge read for fans.
A son writes to his mother who cannot read, about family and violence; a lyrical, short debut by a poet.
After a war that destroyed reality, a man travels to put out a fire; funny and odd.
A narrator reflects on memory, love and society across seven volumes; famously long and demanding yet widely revered.
Fifteen stories of ordinary life in Dublin; short and precise, ending with a famous long one.
The true story of the Donner Party's ill-fated overland journey; recommended as a non-fiction page-turner.
A girl sails a sea of spores to rescue the boy she loves; whimsical and charming.
Old gods fight new ones in modern America; a solid road-trip novel that many prefer to the TV series.
Victorian pickpockets and a heiress get mixed in a plot with major twists; a favourite of many readers.
Seniors join the army to fight aliens in new young bodies; quick and fun, though sequels weaken.
A civil servant looks after a man from Franklin's lost expedition brought to the present; a time-travel romance.
The singer's tender memoir of her friendship with Robert Mapplethorpe in 1970s New York; moving and beautifully written.
A teenage boy wanders New York after leaving school; a short coming-of-age classic readers still enjoy.
A reporter returns to her hometown to cover murders and confronts her family; a gripping, disturbing thriller.
A proud Igbo man's world is upended by colonisers; short and powerful, often read as an answer to colonial fiction.
An angel and a demon try to stop the apocalypse because they like Earth; hilarious and widely loved.
A human raised by Martians returns to Earth and shakes up its customs; a famous, provocative counterculture classic.
A violent outcast lives in the Tennessee hills; short and harrowing, for readers who can handle disturbing McCarthy.
The Roman emperor's private notes on duty, calm and death; readers value its practical stoic advice.

books.t: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
books.why: The story of the woman whose cells were taken without consent and used in science; moving and informative.
A naive young man travels through disaster after disaster while told that all is for the best; short and biting.
A journalist becomes obsessed with a gourmet woman convicted of murder; food, gender and appetite make it hard to stop.
A man is slowly turning into a shark as his wife prepares to lose him; strange, tender and loved by readers.
A broken soldier becomes tutor to a princess in a kingdom cursed by gods; deeply human and well liked.
A torturer, a barbarian and a vain swordsman are drawn into a war; grim and funny, the start of The First Law.
A bookstore clerk stalks a woman and tells it as love; creepy, addictive thriller.
A royal bastard is trained as a secret killer; slow-building and emotional, the first Farseer book.
A woman becomes nanny to two children who burst into flames; absurd, warm and quick, making readers laugh out loud.
One day in the life of a London woman and a shell-shocked soldier; stream of consciousness that some love.
An undercover agent addicted to a drug watches himself; paranoid and sad, someone's comfort book.
A midwestern family comes together for a last Christmas; funny and moving, though compared to DeLillo.
A lonely man kidnaps a young woman and keeps her in his cellar; a short, chilling psychological novel.
A man born at India's independence is linked to other children with powers; colourful and demanding magical realism.
A narrator chases a girl through a world freezing under ice; short, dreamlike and experimental.
A game master is sent to play an alien empire's brutal game; a smart and approachable Culture novel.
A girl turned into an old woman moves into a wizard's castle; funny and charming, different from the film.
Aliens save the last humans but ask for a price; thoughtful, uneasy and often recommended.
A family saga from an African village into American slavery; readers say it is one of the most powerful books they read.
A teenager is tortured by her guardian and neighbourhood kids in 1950s suburbia; the book that broke readers, with an extremely disturbing story.
An elderly minister writes a long letter to his young son; quiet, spiritual and beautifully written.
A farm boy, a princess and a swordfight through fairy-tale perils; witty and loved even more than the movie.
People live in an underground silo and the sheriff wants the truth; gripping with twists, and the basis of Silo.
A quest for the secret of immortality involving beets, perfume and gods; a funny, quirky book readers re-read yearly.
A war orphan wins a place at an elite military school and discovers shamanic power; brutal, exceptional start to a series.
Friends in 1980s Chicago face the AIDS crisis, and one's daughter searches for her family in 2015; left readers shattered.
A family finds a burial ground that brings the dead back; one of the bleakest King novels.
A wife returns from a deep-sea mission changed; short, strange and lyrical.
A shape-shifter spy joins a war between the Culture and its enemies; big, action-driven space opera.
A southern man confronts his family's secrets with his sister's psychiatrist; a long, emotional Southern novel.
A wife in 1890s Louisiana seeks independence; short and ahead of its time, and some readers say it changed their life.
A gang of thieves in a Venice-like city gets pulled into a deadly plot; fast, funny fantasy heist and five-star read.
A bored boy drives into a land of puns and wordplay; clever, loved children's fantasy.
The musician writes about losing her mother and her Korean heritage through food; moving and easy to read.
A mysterious millionaire throws parties to win back his love in Jazz Age New York; short and beautifully written.
Linked stories about humans colonising Mars; lyrical and wistful rather than technical.
A brother and sister are cast out of their family mansion and remain obsessed with it; warm and gently moving.

books.t: The Priory of the Orange Tree
books.why: Dragons and queens in a standalone high fantasy with a sweeping plot; long but fast.
The author's poor Irish childhood in Limerick; sad and often darkly funny, and a bestselling memoir.
An orphan receives a mysterious fortune and learns what matters; one of the most readable Dickens novels.
Two sisters uncover secrets about a serial killer; a gripping, graphic thriller that readers could not put down.
A village girl is taken by a wizard to fight a corrupted wood; a fairy-tale inspired novel that gets absorbing.
Scientists investigate a mysterious spacecraft on the ocean floor; long and gripping, though some find it minor Crichton.
A well-meaning matchmaker misreads everyone around her; light and witty, and free to read.
A family's connection with fairies unfolds over generations; poetic and strange with a following.
A girl volunteers for a televised fight to the death; fast and gripping young-adult dystopia.

books.t: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
books.why: A broad history of humankind from the cognitive revolution on; readers call it excellent, though some dispute its science.
A near-future institution works to fight climate change; ideas-heavy and told in many fragments, often recommended.
Linked stories about people rejected in love and in life; sharp, bold and laugh-out-loud.
Sam Vimes is thrown back to his younger days during a revolt; often named the best Discworld book.
The author's memoir of an abusive relationship, told in short, shifting genre chapters; inventive and powerful.
The Ankh-Morpork night watch faces a dragon; a funny, approachable start to the Watch series.
The true story of a young man who went alone into Alaska; gripping and often recommended.
The wrath of Achilles during the siege of Troy; ancient and brutal epic that readers take on in a good translation.
A lonely young woman working at a prison in 1960s New England meets a stranger; dark and sharp.
A boy's summer in 1928 small-town Illinois, full of wonder; nostalgic and lyrical, from a legitimate genius.
A woman uncovers what may be a secret postal conspiracy in California; short, strange and a good first Pynchon.
Women suddenly gain the ability to shock, flipping the balance of power; compelling and brutal.
A creeping gothic haunted-house story in 1950s Mexico that readers find genuinely disturbing and hard to forget.
Two grieving brothers and the women in their lives, told in Rooney's spare style; fans of her earlier books enjoy it.
A dark fairy tale about a boy who is offered a perfect house of endless holidays and the price attached.
A mother tells her daughters about her youthful acting summer and an old romance; warm and easy, though not for everyone.
Interwoven stories of urban Native Americans in Oakland building toward a powerful finale that left readers in tears.
A teenage cowboy rides into Mexico in a lyrical coming-of-age western praised for its beautiful prose.

books.t: The First Fifteen Lives of Harry August
books.why: A man who relives his life again and again investigates a threat to the world in a clever take on immortality.
A reader-praised novel by Powers set around the ocean and its people, enjoyed more as a story than as typical literary fiction.
A multigenerational saga of twin brothers raised in an Ethiopian hospital, with medicine, family and a gripping story.
A harrowing wartime tale of a boy wandering rural Eastern Europe, remembered as nightmarish and unforgettable.
A professor's family life and fear of death in consumer America, both absurdly funny and deeply unsettling.
A hostage drama set among opera lovers in a South American mansion; beautiful but slow-paced according to some readers.
A failing novelist travels the world to dodge his ex's wedding in a delightful comic novel that lifts reading slumps.
Austen's quiet second-chance love story, often named her best for its mature heroine and gentle feeling.

books.t: The Heart is a Lonely Hunter
books.why: Lonely people in a small Southern town in the 1930s, bound by a deaf-mute man; a classic of Southern gothic.
A short philosophical fable for adults and children about love, loneliness and what matters.
The true story of young women poisoned by radium paint in factories and their fight for justice.
A survivor watches civilisation fall and slowly rebuild after a plague, a quiet pioneering post-apocalyptic novel.
A queer, genre-blending story of a violin teacher, a donut-shop owner and a space-faring secret, praised as unexpected.
Two Black women's friendship and its breaking in a small Ohio town, short and heartbreaking.
A broken Southern family saga told in dense, tangled prose; admired as Faulkner's masterwork but demanding.
A nested story of sisters, a scandal and a pulp novel within the novel, with a long slow-burning twist.
The stars vanish from the sky and time on Earth speeds up; big ideas wrapped around human characters.
An American double agent in World War II and the moral cost of pretending; short and powerful Vonnegut.
A young witch fights a fairy queen with the help of tiny blue men; a funny, warm Discworld entry for young readers.
An investigation of fundamentalist Mormon violence that also examines faith, favoured by readers who like gripping true crime.
The final book of King's gunslinger epic, recommended by fans of the whole series as his big life's work.
A sweeping Civil War romance centred on Scarlett O'Hara, long and compelling though its views are controversial.
A short story of a woman losing her mind under confinement, widely read for its portrait of how women were treated.
The astonishing story of the Theranos fraud, told as a gripping page-turner that works well as an audiobook.
A Black man's search for his family's past and himself, favoured by readers as their top Morrison.
Letters and life of a Black woman in the American South; moving and widely read, with strong praise.
A god stuck as a tortoise and a novice questioning the Church; one of the funniest and sharpest Discworld books.
Four retirees solve cold cases in a care home; cosy, character-driven and easy, though not to every taste.

pl.t: The Last Devil To Die. The Thursday Murder Club 4

books.why: Space opera with deep time, ancient horrors and grim crews; hard sci-fi fans re-read the whole series.

books.t: The Last House on Needless Street
books.why: A strange, twisty horror-thriller about a reclusive man and the haunted house he lives in.
The story of the Great Migration of Black Americans from the South, told through three people's lives.
A domestic thriller about a maid in a wealthy home, a fast hook even for readers who dislike its style.
A woman lives the same life again and again across the first half of the 20th century; some wept at the end.
A woman scientist in the 1960s is pushed into a cooking show; light, funny and warm.
A soldier's training and war against alien bugs; a classic of military sci-fi and a source of many arguments.
Stalkers sneak into a zone left by alien visitors to find artefacts; moving, strange and short.
The King Arthur legend retold with humour and sadness, with a whimsical first part and darker later parts.
A giant, absurd comic novel by the filmmaker about a failing critic and a vast memory-based conspiracy.
A tale of revolutionaries and moral collapse in provincial Russia; some readers name it Dostoevsky's best.
A poor pearl diver finds a great pearl and loses everything; brief and unforgettable, widely read at school.
A woman reckons with an abusive relationship with a teacher; hard to read but sticks with readers.
Four Native American men are hunted by a vengeful spirit after an old hunting crime; vivid horror.
Dickens's long satire of the legal system, whose huge cast and plots reward patient readers.
A strange, comic Vonnegut novel about a car dealer and a sci-fi writer; one of his stranger books.
An uncompromising architect hero and a philosophy of selfishness; loved by some young readers, loathed by others.
Essays about learning French and growing up, praised as laugh-out-loud funny.
A virtual-reality treasure hunt packed with 1980s pop culture; fun, easy and a nostalgic page-turner.
A shy woman defies her family in a century-old romance that readers call lighthearted and still moving.
A hunter finds drug money and is chased by a killer in a sparse, violent modern western.

pl.t: To nie jest kraj dla starych ludzi

books.why: A surreal comic tale of a man, a murder and a strange police station; weird and rewarding for patient readers.
A mysterious sleepwalking plague and a trek across America; readers praise its plot, if not the prose.
A Nebraska immigrant girl's growing up on the prairie, with beautiful, quiet prose that readers return to.
Two boys in a boarding school in the First World War fall in love; harrowing, beautiful and tense.
Short essays rating different parts of the human world on a five-star scale; the chapter on sunsets is a favourite.
A prison guard on death row and a miraculous inmate; King's story that made readers cry.
A wild cyberpunk story of a man seeking his sister in a drug-like virtual world, strange and heart-wrenching.

books.t: The moon is a harsh mistress
books.why: A rebel moon colony fights Earth with the help of a self-aware computer; an enduring Heinlein classic.
A couple's drive to meet his parents spirals into dread; a quick, twisty read with a strange finale.
A vast dark fantasy of hidden worlds, desire and magic; long and strange, and gripping from the first pages.
Six friends' inner lives in poetic, stream-of-consciousness prose; beautiful but demanding, loved by readers of experimental fiction.
Ted Chiang's thoughtful short science fiction about time, free will and consciousness, picked as a favourite story collection.
A boy in 1980s Glasgow cares for his alcoholic mother; devastating and beautifully written.
A breezy adventure about people protecting giant monsters on a parallel Earth; just fun, with quick, witty writing.
A stonemason's doomed struggle against class and marriage in Victorian England, grim and moving.
A long coming-of-age story of an orphan with a club foot, called one of the best books by readers.
An insider's account of working at Facebook, interesting and eye-opening for many readers.
A near-future surveillance state and an interrogation across layered stories; complex but rewarding for fans of puzzle plots.
A novel where a writer's life and her creations intertwine; a recent release that readers enjoyed.
A fictional take on a real convicted murderess, told through her memory; Atwood's literary mystery.
A boy narrates a post-nuclear England in invented broken English; underrated, odd and moving.
A Romanian teacher's mundane life collides with surreal visions in a huge, brilliant dreamlike novel.
A disfigured model's twisted road trip in this wild, transgressive novel.
A woman physician in Ming-dynasty China fights for her place; engrossing historical fiction on women's lives.
A funny, fascinating tour of what happens to human bodies after death, praised as laugh-out-loud science writing.
A girl enters a strange institute where reality bends and she is slowly transformed; readers re-read it yearly.
A celebrity memoir read cover to cover in one day by fans who found it gripping.
A cozy afterlife tale about a man who runs a tea shop for the dead; warm and good for grief.
A WWII nurse is thrown back to 18th-century Scotland; a huge romantic saga with devoted fans.
An Irish man gains immortality as long as he stays in New York, tracing the city's history.
A vast crumbling castle and its rigid inhabitants, written in rich, long sentences; a gothic classic of fantasy.
Explorers visit an enormous artificial ring with a strange civilisation; a hard-SF classic of big ideas.
A wartime love story told in letters; an ugly-cry read for those who like emotional romance.
A boy finds a book that takes him to a magical world, much richer than the film; a child's fantasy classic.
A detective chases a villain who steals characters from books in an alternate England; funny and clever for bookworms.
A sled dog turns wild in the Klondike gold rush; short, easy and a favourite classic.
A wife vanishes and secrets unravel in a twisty thriller with unlikeable characters that readers dissect.
A short reality-bending sci-fi adventure that readers praise as a taste of Reynolds's writing.
A slow-building fantasy of a young man's service to a legendary emperor, loved for its heart and humour.
A land under a sorcerer's curse, a war of memory; admired for glorious prose even if some plots bother readers.
A memoir of the year after her husband's sudden death and the irrational ways grief works.
A moneylender's daughter in a wintry Eastern European world, a clever fairy-tale retelling with multiple narrators.

books.t: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
books.why: A bounty hunter hunts androids in a ruined world and asks what makes someone human; the book behind Blade Runner.
A society woman falls out of favour in New York's Gilded Age; tragic and beautifully written.
Secret societies at Yale deal in dark magic, with a harsh mystery that hooks readers.
A lawyer's fight for the wrongly condemned, moving and eye-opening about the US justice system.
A near-future where prisoners fight to the death on TV, praised by critics for its sharp edge and urgency.
A tennis star's honest, surprising life story, great even for those who do not follow tennis.

books.t: All Creatures Great and Small (All Creatures Great and Small #1-2)
books.why: A young Yorkshire vet's warm, funny stories about farms and animals; readers re-read it for comfort.
DeLillo's novel of expatriates in Greece and a cult murdering people; admired by readers who love his cool style.
Three linked tales of two planets and identity; a dreamlike science fiction classic.
An extremely violent, grim comic horror novel; one reader calls it the most unhinged thing they've read.
A boy and his two hunting dogs in the Ozarks; short and tear-jerking.
A poet who changes sex and lives for centuries across English history; playful and demanding.
A delinquent in a violent future England is reconditioned; short and iconic, in invented slang.
Two scholars uncover the secret love of Victorian poets in a rich, layered romance and mystery.
A middle-aged man torn between bourgeois and wild impulses; a great book that some find a difficult read.
The real story of Shackleton's lost ship and crew survival in Antarctica, reads like an adventure novel.
A witch-tale about a goat-legged being in colonial Pennsylvania, illustrated; good Halloween reading.
A chef's blunt, funny memoir of kitchen life, found witty and warm.
An abbess in medieval France builds a world of women in a short, magical-realist novel.
A study of America's hidden caste system, urged by readers who want to understand US history and society.
A family goes on the run in a collapsing near-future America; readers enjoyed it but some withheld judgment.
Expatriates in 1920s Paris and Spain travel, drink and aimlessly drift; Hemingway's famous spare style.
A girl's escape from slavery on a literal railroad; an alternative-history novel that won big awards.
An old woman is the last of her colony and must meet aliens; praised as outstanding by readers.
A wounded Confederate soldier walks home across the Civil War South to his love; poetic and slow.
A teacher's chilling confession opens a revenge story told by several voices; gripping and short.
Three lives intertwine in Appalachian nature in Kingsolver's love of the natural world.
A multigenerational tale of trees and a family across time; many readers name it a current favourite.

books.t: The Narrow Road to the Deep North
books.why: A surgeon on the Burma railway and a love story; harrowing, heartbreaking and prize-winning.
An old couple travels a misty post-Arthurian Britain in search of their son; quiet and moving, about memory.
Two sisters and their strange aunt in a remote lake town; haunting prose beloved by literary fans.
A courtesan spy in a world of intrigue, with deep worldbuilding and heavy themes; the start of a series.
Two women divers on a Korean island over decades, a gripping portrait of friendship; engrossing.
A gunslinger chases the man in black across a desert, opening a strange epic; fans say read the series.
A reluctant soldier in powered armour fights in endless wars; a gritty military SF recommended by veterans of the genre.
A medieval-Spain-inspired world of three peoples, a tale of war, friendship and honour that readers call magnificent.
A thief and a knight travel a grim world with sharp humour and gore; the author-read audiobook has readers laughing aloud.
A near-future story of contact with an intelligent octopus, a hacker and ethics; full of ideas that stay with readers.
A strange, funny novel about a woman who falls for aircraft; absurd but sharp about modern dating.
A near-future thriller where a DNA test matches you to your soulmate; readers were hooked from page one.
The Battle of Gettysburg through the eyes of its generals, a Pulitzer-winning war novel that works even for readers who avoid war fiction.
A strange, tender novel about a girl who believes she is an alien; sublime despite its odd premise.

books.t: Lamb: The Gospel According to Biff, Christ's Childhood Pal
books.why: The missing years of Jesus told by his best friend, with irreverent humour; readers say it hooks from the start.
A retired historian pieces together his grandparents' pioneering life in the American West; slow, rich and rewarding.
A surveyor tries to reach a castle's authorities in endless red tape; odd, funny and full of dread.
A woman awaits execution in 19th-century Iceland, told in beautiful prose; readers recommend anything by Kent.
Butler's grim sequel about a religious fascist America and a prophet's family; not enjoyable but powerful and chillingly relevant.
A serial killer story that is lyrical and gruesome; a one-sitting read that stays in the mind.
A mountain lion narrates a short, strange, poetic novel; readers say it is really good if you accept its vision.
Humans pursue an alien object across deep space and time; the timescales stay in readers' minds for years.
A gold-rush mystery structured by astrology in 1860s New Zealand; long, intricate and absorbing.

books.t: Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas
books.why: A drug-fuelled road trip through Nevada, wildly funny and famously chaotic; a cult classic.

pl.t: Fear and Loathing on the Campaign Trail '72

books.why: A girl survives alone on an island for years; a short children's survival classic readers recommend.
The true crime story of the murders of Osage people for their oil wealth, told like a thriller.
A cynical girl survives a deadly magical school; fast, sharp and ironic.
A salvage diver, a missing passenger and a haunted sister; a tough, odd novel for devoted McCarthy readers.
A racehorse's story links centuries of American history and art; remembered long after finishing.
A prospector gambles on alien-made ships and is haunted by guilt; a classic of classic space SF.
A preacher, a fixation on electricity and the dark where it leads; its final pages impress its fans.
A scavenger finds a living creature in a ruined city ruled by a giant bear; weird, atmospheric and beloved.

books.t: All Quiet on the Western Front
books.why: A German soldier's view of the First World War; bleak, human and timeless anti-war writing.
A pianist arrives in a town where the logic is dream-like; slow, strange and demanding Ishiguro.
A colour-ruled caste society in a strange future Britain; funny, inventive and clever.
A woman's life tangled with a secret war of immortals across decades; sprawling and ambitious.
A near-future climate collapse seen from many angles and characters; a heavy, long novel that readers call a favourite.
Mice defend their abbey from a rat warlord in a classic animal adventure with feasts and bravery.
A lawyer is torn between a proper fiancee and a forbidden love in Gilded Age New York.
An imaginative orphan finds a home on Prince Edward Island; a gentle, funny children's classic.
A Nigerian woman's love story across Lagos, America and Britain; sharp on race and identity.
A single mother raises a genius son by teaching him languages; clever, odd and brilliant.
A tour through how animals sense the world, with creatures' strange perception; readers say it breaks the human-centred view.
The life of the Roman emperor told in letters and documents; praised as Williams's best.
A crew of misfits plans an impossible heist in a fantasy city; described as Ocean's Eleven with magic.
A bored provincial wife's romantic delusions lead to ruin; the standard realist novel.
A vampire-hunter tells his life to a historian in a grim world of monsters; a long book readers can't put down.

books.t: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance
books.why: A motorcycle trip and an inquiry into quality; layered and philosophical, with many readers re-reading it.
A series of interviews tell the story of a zombie war; clever, global and shaped like an oral history.
One bloody battle fought in a few days, with grim comedy and well-drawn soldiers; fans love its brutality.
A boy crosses America and a parallel world to save his dying mother; a King and Straub team-up.
A phone-sex operator listens to a woman's therapy sessions; hilarious, wild and sexual.
A railway worker's life in the early American West, short and lyrical; one reader found it underwhelming.
A girl gets an interactive book that shapes her life in a nano-tech future; clever world-building.
The story of the mad woman in the attic from Jane Eyre, told from her side in the Caribbean.
A prince is framed and the kingdom is in danger in a straightforward medieval fantasy from King.
Crew members on a starship notice their friends keep dying; fans of Star Trek enjoy this light, fast joke.
Four March sisters grow up during the Civil War; warm, much-loved and a good choice for readers young or old.
Descendants of drowned African women live underwater and keep their people's memory; short, moving and haunting.
A bullied teen with telekinesis takes revenge; King's short debut that hooked readers young.
A southern woman moves to a northern mill town and meets a proud manufacturer; romance and social class.
Life among the poor and cheerful residents of a California fishing street; short and warmly written.
A strange and gorgeous space opera with drugs and dread, ranked among readers' top five.
A romantasy with a dangerous love story and fast plot; one reader calls it the best of five years.
The last man on Earth among vampires; the final chapter lingers in readers' minds for years.
Scrooge is visited by three ghosts on Christmas Eve; a short, familiar ghost story that still works for most readers.
A psychologist helps hunt a killer in 1890s New York; far better than the TV series, fans say.
A vast epic series about knights, spren and a world of storms, loved by readers for its worldbuilding.
A security expert explains how to read danger signs and trust your instincts; named required reading.
A lonely orphan finds a hidden garden and heals; a gentle children's classic.
A future of utopian cities and philosophical argument narrated in an 18th-century voice; hard going but rewarding for ambitious readers.
Marco Polo describes imaginary cities to Kublai Khan in short poetic chapters; readers call it mind-blowing.
A boy discovers he is one of the Old Ones who fight the Dark in a wintry English setting; readers return to it.
A woman follows the last Arctic terns across the sea amid extinction; hopeful and sad.
A trickster thief in a far-future Mars city; dense, clever and said to be the best of its kind.
An oral biography of a strange man who spreads a disease; rougher than other Palahniuk but rewarding.
A surgeon looks at ageing and dying and how to give people a better ending; recommended for everyone.
A designer's novel about a signal from space, built as a physical artefact with many documents; fans say it is perfect.
A grim mercenary company's chronicle in a ruthless war; the military fantasy readers recommend if you are bored of Sanderson.
Tiny life forms on a neutron star evolve rapidly, a hard SF classic; readers like the alien idea.
Three lives caught up in the Biafran war in Nigeria; moving and well praised.
A teen in a divided Northern Irish town is stalked by a paramilitary; stream-of-consciousness, tough but excellent.
People in the Mississippi town and a man's outsiderness; one of Faulkner's heavy novels with beauty.
How the Sackler family fuelled the opioid crisis, reported like a drama; depressing but gripping.
A man tries to bring back segregation in his town in a ferociously funny satire.
Two teens survive on an island after a tsunami and rethink faith; funny, brutal and moving.
A hunt for buffalo in 1870s Kansas that grinds the men down; a brutal literary western.
A scientist's microscopic intelligences take over; weird and ahead of its time, more hard SF than horror.
A London policeman discovers magic and a dark ghostly murder; funny paranormal mystery.
A family secret and grief in South Carolina and France; emotionally devastating Southern saga.
A symbologist chases secrets across Europe in a breathless conspiracy thriller; some readers found it mind-blowing.
Sixteen heirs to a rich man are paired to solve his murder; a children's puzzle mystery loved by adults.
A communist double agent after the Vietnam War, told in confession; a Pulitzer winner, darkly funny.
Boys stranded on an island descend into savagery; short classic often read in school.
A dark necromancy and war romance that readers devoured and rated highly.
A vast, experimental novel of a working-class English town across time, with its own languages; rewarding but exhausting.
The Roman emperor's story told with wit and intrigue; easy to read and fun.
A southern horror about two brothers and a nightmare family, with twists and a final chapter that surprises.

books.t: Three Men in a Boat (to say nothing of the dog)
books.why: Three friends and a dog row up the Thames in a comic Victorian classic; still funny.

pl.t: Trzech panów w łódce (nie licząc psa)

books.why: The true story of a prolific art thief, told like a thriller; short and engaging.
Six survivors tell what happened when the atomic bomb fell on Hiroshima; a short reportage classic.
A woman who is diagnosed as a sociopath explains her inner life and how she lives with it.
A girl who reads characters out of books; the first of a trilogy for fantasy-loving children.
A man loses his memory to a creature that eats thoughts; a puzzle-like thriller like Memento.
The life of a writer and his mother, a feminist icon, full of black comedy and tragedy.
The Arthurian legend told from the women's view; a favourite, though readers note problems with its author.
The story of Dinah, a girl from the Bible, told by her; a women's life in the ancient world.

books.t: Stories of Your Life and Others
books.why: Chiang's thoughtful short stories including the basis for Arrival; clever and moving.
Generations of colonists on a distant planet, interacting with intelligent bamboo; praised as a late discovery.
A man discovers a hidden London beneath the city; readers loved it from age 14 on.
A doctor's memoir of a tropical island and what his research caused; unsettling, incredible prose.
A corrupt Edinburgh policeman narrated partly by his tapeworm; filthy, grim and unusual.
A mysterious woman in white, a sinister count and a puzzle; an early Victorian sensation novel.
The first volume of a vast fantasy epic; a favourite among teenage readers who loved the world.
Two families in London over generations; funny, warm and well noted.
King's memoir and writing advice; readers value it as both a life story and a practical guide.
A hard-to-describe vampire story set in New York in the 1970s; fans insist you go in blind.
The history of Salisbury and its area from the Ice Age to modern times, told through families.
A girl in an amphitheatre fights time thieves who steal people's hours; a short fable about valuing time.
A failing man takes his family to a harsh Newfoundland and finds a new life; rich, quirky prose.
A modern writer is guided through a Dante-style hell; a fan favourite among Niven works.
The Buendía family across a century in a town called Macondo; magical realism's best known book.
Engineers live at the bottom of the sea, and the dark gets to them; dark, atmospheric hard SF.
Children enter a world of talking animals and a lion; a lifelong favourite for many readers.
A magical New York across centuries; ornate and moving, though the film failed the book.
A governess and the ghostly children in her care; ambiguous and short, the great ghost story.
A photographer lures men into her flat in a dark, unreliable satire; recommended.
A boy shares a lifeboat with a tiger; a story that makes readers consider belief.
A real samurai's life from violent youth to wise master; recommended to Shogun fans.
One long sentence through a painter's life, faith and death; hard and unforgettable.
A torturer's apprentice in a dying far-future world, written in an elaborate style; first volume of a classic series.
A mercenary-hero's story in a long, beloved space series; readers re-read Bujold often.
A girl is cursed to obey every command in this fairy-tale retelling; a favourite from childhood.
Humans and a mysterious alien world meet in this recent Tchaikovsky novel; the author is a modern favourite.
Linked stories of drug-ridden misfits with rare grace; strange but moving.
A baker in a world of vampires gets involved in a mess; makes you hungry for baked goods.
Milton's epic poem of Satan's fall and the Fall of man; amazing and tough.
Two widowers go fishing at a haunted creek and hear a terrifying tale; readers say it stays with them.
A planet with a strange ecology and a diplomat-led investigation; fans re-read it periodically.
Generations of Danish seafarers in a spanning saga of sea and home; an epic that readers love.
The rock musician's lively life stories, best in the audiobook he reads himself.
The actor's moving account of poverty and rising to success, with a gripping audiobook she narrates.

books.t: Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil
books.why: A true-crime portrait of Savannah and its eccentric residents, read as a travel-style and murder tale.
A woman flees an abusive marriage in a bold early feminist novel; readers pair it with the Brontë classics.
An alien visits Earth to stop a mathematical breakthrough and learns to love humans; funny and touching.
A girl conceived to save her sister sues for control of her body; a gripping family drama.
Humans first meet aliens, and have to decide what to do about them; an old-school classic.
The final instalment of the Red Rising trilogy, a fast, violent space opera for fans.
A history professor writes a book on Nazi Germany and gets lost in his own house; a huge postmodern work.
A dying professor's final talk on living, which made readers reflect on their own lives.
An unlikely friendship between a young man and an elderly woman in a small American town.
An American fighter joins guerrillas in the Spanish Civil War; a classic of war fiction.
A detective revisits a childhood trauma in an Irish forest; hooks readers with atmosphere.
Death takes an apprentice in a funny, clever Discworld novel and an easy place to begin.
An Anishinaabe community faces winter after the grid falls; short, tense and quietly powerful.

books.t: Perfume: The Story of a Murderer
books.why: A man with a perfect sense of smell kills to create the ultimate scent; strange and gripping.
A lonely English teacher abroad in a French town; slow, cold and psychologically sharp.
A girl in the South copes with abuse and poverty; raw, painful and powerful.
The history of Middle-earth in a biblical style, dry for some readers but rich for devoted fans.
The first settlers build Mars and fight over its future; a detailed, imaginative work of colonisation.
A native man tells the fall of the Aztec empire in lively detail; a favourite for many readers.
French coal miners strike in the 1860s; far from boring, readers found it gripping and humane.
A woman loses her whole family in the 2004 tsunami and writes about grief; hauntingly beautiful.
Eighteen linked tales shown through a man's tattoos; a collection by a writer many call a genius.
A poor girl's fall in rural Victorian England; tragic, with grim scenes readers still discuss.
The aftermath of nuclear war in a small Florida town; dated in places but gripping.
A man goes to a ghost town to find his father; ghostly and short, with jumpy storytelling that readers value.
A huge, strange western with experimental typography; readers urge others to try it.
A near-future family at sea after a climate collapse; readers who liked other climate fiction recommend it.
A young wizard learns the cost of power in a short, wise fantasy classic.

books.t: The Ten Thousand Doors of January
books.why: A girl finds a book that opens doors to other worlds; lyrical and magical.

books.a: Robert Shea and Robert Anton Wilson
books.why: Conspiracy theories and secret societies, a chaotic and satirical cult favourite; recommended by those who want something weird.
The childhood of the future abbess in early medieval Britain, vivid and richly detailed; its sequel is also praised.
A prequel to The Hunger Games about Haymitch, which readers are eagerly reading.
A teenage Barrayaran gets entangled in a spiralling mercenary scheme; fast, funny space opera.
A robot butler continues its duties after a crisis; slow to begin but ends with clever pay-offs.
Backpackers seek a hidden island paradise that goes wrong; praised as one of the best by one reader.
Robert Langdon chases another puzzle, with a conspiracy theory; a guilty-pleasure thriller for fans.
An overpopulated near future told through fragmented media; a landmark of New Wave SF.
A Culture novel about virtual hells and a war over them; the idea stuck in readers' minds for years.
Two teenagers with cancer fall in love; an easy tear-jerker.
Children hidden away in an attic in a dark gothic family drama that earned a cult following.
A boy raised by ghosts in a graveyard; with a memorable opening line.
A Pulitzer winner turns to the zombie apocalypse with a thoughtful, literary survivor.
A sprawling Pynchon epic with anarchists, airships and genius moments; one of his hardest books.
A murder mystery in a fantasy empire with a political twist; some readers think about it daily.
A diver goes down a mysterious ocean trench and then to the farthest reaches; an unusual literary sci-fi.
A Culture novel about ancient artefact and ship Minds' games; re-read by many fans.
Three generations ride the technological singularity; dense with ideas and not for everyone.

books.t: Journey to the end of the night
books.why: A cynical young man's wandering through war, colonies and poverty; foul, funny and revolutionary.

books.t: The Ocean at the End of the Lane
books.why: A man returns to his childhood home and recalls a strange girl and her pond; short and spellbinding.
Old people feed on others' violence in a long, grim horror; fans say it is a top vampire novel.

books.t: In the Heart of the Sea
books.why: The true story of the whaleship Essex sunk by a whale; a quick, absorbing page-turner.
Two French priests in 19th-century New Mexico; gentle, quiet and beautiful.
Ignatius Reilly, a slothful medievalist, causes chaos in New Orleans; a laugh per page.
Becky Sharp climbs the Regency social ladder in this long satire; some readers need two attempts.
A noblewoman is left on an island by her relatives in the 1500s; readers found it very good.
A boy grows up in South Africa and learns boxing amid apartheid; a long coming-of-age classic.
Dick's strange religious experience turned into a novel; readers need caveats but love its oddness.
Seven pilgrims tell their stories on the way to a shrine; a landmark with horror in its pages.
A city on rails moves up a world that never stops, with a surprising twist; readers dreamed of it for weeks.
A fast techno-thriller where historians are sent back to 14th-century France; readers enjoy its pacing and blend of research and adventure.
A WWII tale of a captured spy and her pilot friend, praised for its friendship and a story that rewards close attention.
A drifting young woman cons her way through a Long Island summer; readers find it unsettling and impossible to put down.
A grieving mother raises a creature grown from her dead son, mixing light horror with a moving story about loss.
Tina Fey's comic memoir of comedy writing and career; readers recall the laugh-out-loud cruise ship anecdote in particular.

books.t: The Very Secret Society of Irregular Witches
books.why: A gentle, romantic witch story with a found-family feel, recommended as comforting bedtime reading.
A harrowing novel of a young Black man in 1930s Chicago; widely read in school and remembered for its force.
Jenny Lawson's memoir of an odd childhood and anxiety, recommended for being relentlessly funny.
A weird, inventive fantasy set on a floating city of ships, loved for its world-building within the Bas-Lag series.
A short story of a lonely dreamer in St Petersburg who falls for a girl over four nights; readers feel its sad hopelessness.
Sagan's case for scientific thinking against superstition and pseudoscience, recommended as a clear, humane guide to skepticism.
A murdered girl watches her family cope from heaven; readers recall it as heartbreaking and unforgettable.
A huge, almost entirely dialogue-driven satire of American money about a schoolboy running a business empire; praised as brilliant but demanding.
A novella of four boys hiking to find a dead body, recommended for its nostalgia and coming-of-age feel.
An apocalypse seen through a cantankerous crow and his dog companion; readers like the humour mixed with heart.
Wells's short classic about a traveller journeying to a far future; recommended for its ideas and brevity.
A short King story about teleportation and its terrible catch; readers call it dark and effective.
Ender's sequel is a thoughtful story about empathy and first contact; many prefer it to the original.
A 1950s road novel following young men across America; readers find it warm, vivid and gripping.
Virginia Giuffre's memoir about abuse and her fight for justice; readers describe it as powerful and hard to forget.
A horse narrates his life under kind and cruel owners; a gentle children's classic many remember from childhood.
A nurse cares for a woman accused of murdering her family in a creepy mansion; a page-turning thriller favourite.
A scientist exiled to an alien world studies its bizarre life; recommended as strong hard science fiction.
Wyndham's tale of telepathic children hiding in a post-nuclear community that persecutes mutations; short and gripping.
Three women in different centuries share a bond with nature and face persecution; recommended for its multi-generational story.
A golem and a jinni meet in 1900s New York; readers love its characters and gentle, immigrant-centred magic.
A detailed account of the 1937 massacre in Nanking; readers call it among the most disturbing books they have read.
A poet recounts crossing from El Salvador to the US at age nine; readers find it powerful and moving.
The second Earthsea book follows a young priestess in a desert temple; praised as a haunting, tight fantasy.
An Australian federal agent returns to a drought-stricken town to investigate a killing; recommended as a gripping mystery.
In a world without death, scythes must kill to control population; a fast YA series starter teens and adults enjoy.

books.t: The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time
books.why: A teenager with autism investigates a neighbour's dead dog; readers like its distinctive narrator and quick pace.
A family saga about four sisters and the man who joins them; readers recommend it as a touching, warm read.
Swashbuckling classic of d'Artagnan and his friends in 17th-century France; recommended as fun adventure.
Vonnegut's satire of a rich man giving away his fortune out of kindness; praised as funny and humane.
A dense novel about uploaded minds and simulated worlds; hard-SF fans call it the definitive take on the concept.
A librarian runs a magical shop on a quiet island; readers call it sweet, cosy and perfect for bedtime.
Franzen's novel of a 1970s Midwestern family in crisis; readers found it surprisingly good and engrossing.
A narrator's mind travels through the cosmos and the history of the universe; recommended for its sheer scale.
A village cuts itself off during the 1666 plague; readers praise its human drama and vivid detail.
Michelle Obama's memoir from her Chicago childhood to the White House; recommended as honest and inspiring.
The true story of a KGB officer who spied for Britain; reads like a thriller and is highly recommended.

books.t: The Man in the High Castle
books.why: A world where the Axis won WWII; Dick's classic alternate history is recommended for its unsettling mood.
An orphan raised in a Maine orphanage grapples with the doctor's moral code; readers call it a favourite.
A child murder case with impossible evidence blends police procedure and the supernatural; best for King fans.
A Booker-winning New Zealand novel about three damaged people forming a family; intense, poetic and unforgettable.
A teenager blackmails a hidden Nazi war criminal in a novella readers remember as truly horrifying.
A girl in a colonial outpost is swept into a desert kingdom's war; a beloved comfort fantasy.
Twin sisters take diverging paths, one passing as white, and their daughters' lives echo it; praised and widely read.
A noir detective story in a future where minds are swapped between bodies; recommended as gritty cyberpunk.
A short Gothic vampire novella that predates Dracula; recommended as a classic of atmospheric horror.
Vonnegut's satire narrated a million years in the future about how humanity ends up evolving; quirky and funny.
A 300-year saga of loggers and forests across generations; readers describe it as an epic, educational novel about trees.

books.t: One Day, Everyone Will Have Always Been Against This
books.why: Omar El Akkad's essay-memoir on the West's response to Gaza, called one of the year's most powerful books.

books.t: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
books.why: Four children enter a snowbound magical land in Lewis's classic fantasy; a childhood favourite recommended for comfort reading.
A darker, political retelling of the Wicked Witch of the West's life; quite different from the musical.
A drifter revives the postal service in a post-apocalyptic America; nothing like the film and recommended for its hopeful tone.
Tuchman's account of the opening month of WWI is called suspenseful and the definitive study of how war broke out.
A vampire tells his life story to a reporter; recommended as a lush, influential Gothic horror novel.
A conman is forced to run the failing Ankh-Morpork post office; one of the funnier, accessible Discworld books.
A Laguna Pueblo war veteran seeks healing through tradition; praised as a deeply moving Native American novel.
A WWI soldier hears an angel in no man's land, told in a breathless run-on style readers found striking.
Two Jesuit priests face persecution in 17th-century Japan; a profound novel about faith and doubt.
A comet strikes Earth and survivors rebuild; recommended as a classic disaster novel with a large cast.
Sagan's tour of the universe and our place in it; readers say it changes how they see life.
Mailer's massive true-crime account of killer Gary Gilmore's final months; recommended as a landmark of nonfiction.
An elderly man in a small town befriends strangers by buying their art; readers call it a heartwarming read.
A short, warm tale of robots running a noodle restaurant after an upheaval; recommended as a quick, gentle science fiction read.
A Kentucky woman drives west and ends up raising an abandoned child in Arizona; readers remember it fondly.
