A reclusive author tells a biographer her gothic family story; recommended as a compelling book-lover's mystery.
A sprawling story of friendship and found family spanning Florence and London across decades; warm and humane.
A letter from Coates to his teenage son about growing up Black in America; readers call it both loving and devastating.
A medieval siege story mixing historical fiction, fantasy and horror; readers pick it as a dark, claustrophobic read.
Asimov's linked stories on robots and the Three Laws; recommended as a foundational, idea-rich classic of science fiction.
Ann Patchett's new novel is praised by early readers as engrossing and easy to love, even on a long flight.
A sheltered woman uncovers her strange past after her father's death; read in one sitting by many fans.
Hesse's coming-of-age story of self-discovery; one reader says it changed their life at seventeen.
A short novella about astronauts studying distant worlds; a favourite for its warmth and wonder.
A woman escapes a kidnapper in a relentless chase; readers remember it as terrifying.
A town is trapped under an invisible barrier and turns on itself; a gripping, gruesome King epic.
Survivors face Bigfoot after a volcano isolates their eco-community; readers found it spooky and unputdownable.
A young woman raised on a militarist space station faces the truth; a Hugo-winning novel readers enjoyed.
Borges's brainy short stories on labyrinths, libraries and invented worlds; recommended for mind-bending ideas.
A man steps into 1880s New York through a secret government project; a time-travel classic readers enjoy.
A botanist's life across the nineteenth century, from Cook's voyages to science and love; praised and sweeping.
A gifted accountant infiltrates an empire to bring it down; recommended as political fantasy with painful choices.
The conclusion of Simmons's Hyperion story, about AI and the fate of humanity; recommended alongside the first book.

books.t: The Thousand Autumns of Jacob de Zoet
books.why: A Dutch clerk at Dejima in 1799 Japan; an epic readers value for its richness.
Salinger's pair of stories about a troubled family and spiritual crisis; one reader calls it a favourite.

books.t: The Clan of the Cave Bear
books.why: A Cro-Magnon girl raised by Neanderthals in prehistoric Europe; the first of a six-book series, recommended for immersive reading.
A true-crime account of three sisters abused by their mother; readers say it is horrifying and hard to put down.
Two light-skinned Black women meet again in 1920s Harlem and one passes as white; a short, tense classic.
A family saga mixing religion, baseball and the Vietnam War in the Pacific Northwest; loved by those who read it.
In a world where teens can be harvested, three runaways try to survive; a quick, unsettling YA read.
A journalist works for a populist Southern governor; a Pulitzer-winning novel about power and corruption.
Death takes over the Hogfather's job in a Discworld story about belief and what makes us human.
A detective and a ship's officer chase a conspiracy across the solar system; a fast start to the Expanse series.
A graphic memoir of growing up in Iran during revolution and war; readers praise its honesty and humour.
Spiegelman's graphic memoir of his father's Holocaust survival with mice as characters; widely recommended as essential.
Tourists trapped on a jungle hill face a malign plant; readers found it so intense they had to skip pages.

books.t: The Art of Racing in the Rain
books.why: A dog narrates his racing driver owner's life and family troubles; a tearjerker readers love.
Mann's family saga of a German merchant dynasty in decline; recommended for readers wanting a long classic.
Vampires on a Mississippi steamboat in the 1850s; recommended as a rich, Twain-flavoured Gothic horror.
Joe Simpson's true story of surviving a fall in the Andes; readers call it suspenseful, tragic and almost unbelievable.

books.t: Everyone in This Room Will Someday Be Dead
books.why: An anxious, atheist woman takes a job at a church; readers love its dark humour and heart.
Lewis's retelling of Cupid and Psyche through a jealous sister, very different from Narnia.
A Victorian novel about a stolen diamond, often called the first detective story; readers find it engrossing.
Four Chinese-American mothers and daughters share their stories; readers recommend it for multi-generational family drama.
A short mix of fantasy and science fiction about a lonely sorceress and an outsider; quick and strong.
A soldier relives the same war in broken time; fans praise its anti-militarist edge, though some found it hard to follow.
Rushdie's magical-realist novel about two Indian actors, famous for the fatwa; dense but highly regarded.

books.t: The Rise and Fall of the Third Reich
books.why: Shirer's massive account of Nazi Germany; readers treat it as a classic and parallel for modern times.

pl.t: The Rise and Fall of the Third Reich: a History of Nazi Germany

books.why: Vonnegut's debut imagines a society run by machines and engineers; praised as a satirical, humane dystopia.
A man relives one day in different bodies to solve a murder at a country house; a puzzle readers enjoy.
A free-roaming dog narrates his days in a park; a great new, warm, adventurous read for both kids and adults.
A love-triangle story spanning college days and later life; called really great, moving and an easy read.
A haunted IKEA-style store where staff face a night shift of horrors; a wild, funny and chaotic ride.

books.t: The years of rice and salt
books.why: An alternate history where Europe's plague wiped out nearly everyone and the world went another way; ambitious and sweeping.
A satirical novel about a marriage and modern obsessions with health; one reader rated it ten out of ten.
A boy joins a pirate treasure hunt; a not-heavy adventure classic recommended as a great story.
An old man and a girl are tied together by a lost manuscript; readers go back to it repeatedly.
A small town is changed by a buried spacecraft; fun sci-fi horror from King.
DeLillo's fictional take on Lee Harvey Oswald and the Kennedy assassination; readers who liked White Noise seek it out.
The first Discworld novel, a madcap parody of fantasy; fans enjoy it though many suggest starting elsewhere in the series.
The dense, unexplained start of the Malazan series; recommended as straight-up swords and magic for patient fantasy fans.

books.t: The Spirit Catches You and You Fall Down
books.why: A Hmong child's epilepsy shows the clash between American medicine and her family's beliefs; readers remember it long after.
All technology suddenly stops working and survivors in Oregon fight to rebuild; an engaging post-apocalyptic start to a series.
Dahl's story of a clever girl with telekinetic powers and awful grown-ups; a beloved childhood read.
Kids with special abilities are held in a secret facility; a gripping King thriller one reader finished in a weekend.
A stay-at-home mother believes she is turning into a dog; readers see it as a sharp metaphor for motherhood.
A fictional telling of the Battle of Thermopylae from a Spartan squire's view; readers say it moved them deeply.
A lawyer defends her husband accused of murder in this twisty thriller; readers wish they could read it fresh again.
A young man is swallowed by a sperm whale and must survive inside it; NPR-endorsed, gripping and surprisingly emotional.
Du Maurier's novel about whether a widow is a murderer or an innocent; readers love its ambiguity.
McCarthy's early grim, Gothic tale of a brother and sister in the rural South; bleak and powerful.
A farmer's wife is torn between husband and an old love in post-war England; readers say it is moving and unputdownable.
An amnesiac woman discovers she runs a secret supernatural agency in Britain; a quirky, fun ride.
A farm boy finds a dragon egg in the first Inheritance Cycle book; an easy fantasy adventure for young readers.
Tolle's guide to living in the present; readers say it changed their lives and helped them stop overthinking.
Rilke's ten letters of advice to a young writer on solitude and creating; readers find it timeless and inspiring.
A frustrated Black novelist writes a parody that becomes a hit; a sharp satire on publishing and race.
Atwood's sequel to The Handmaid's Tale told by three women inside Gilead; recommended as gripping dystopian fiction.
A book of personal essays about how reading changes our lives, recommended for writers of memoir.
Roberts's early science fiction about two colonies on a salt planet at war; a reader enjoyed it.
Stories of ordinary North Koreans; reads like gripping fiction and gives a rare look at daily life.
A boy narrates his family's flight across the Midwest after his brother is accused of murder; loved for its prose.
A concierge and a precocious girl find beauty in a Paris building; a gentle book about hidden depths.
Two potters in Syracuse stage Greek plays with Athenian prisoners; praised as funny, moving and unusual.
Michener's sprawling saga of a Colorado town across centuries, rooted in geology and history.
A woman travels between parallel Earths where her other selves are dead; recommended along with its sequel.
James Clear's practical book on forming good habits through small changes; recommended even by self-help sceptics.
An Irish girl emigrates to 1950s Brooklyn and must choose between two homes; a quiet, moving novel.
A beta male becomes a death merchant in San Francisco; a comic fantasy readers say made them laugh hard.
The actress who played Nellie Oleson tells of her childhood fame and abuse; recommended as frank and funny.
Pamuk's novel about a poet in a snowbound Turkish border town; recommended as a political, thoughtful literary read.
Jenny Lawson's memoir on mental illness told with wild humour; readers call her uproariously funny.
Diamond's argument that geography explains the unequal spread of power; one reader calls it the best book they have read.
Undset's trilogy of one woman's life in medieval Norway; readers recommend it as a vast, rewarding classic.
A very short story about death and the nature of life; readers find it brief but excellent.
Dante's journey through hell, purgatory and paradise; readers recommend translations such as Ciardi's.
A strange, dreamlike post-apocalyptic story told by a young man; fans of Gene Wolfe often list it among favourites.
A ten-volume epic fantasy starting with Gardens of the Moon; demanding, but fans rank it among the best.
Scientists race to contain a deadly microbe from space; a classic techno-thriller readers still enjoy.
Dragonriders defend a planet from deadly Thread; readers call it a brilliant series, starting with Dragonflight.
A bookshop is haunted during the 2020 pandemic and the Minneapolis protests; praised and loved by Erdrich fans.
A convict struggles to survive in a far-future prison and a dying Earth; praised for its prose and worldbuilding.
A set of weird stories linked by a cursed play; a classic for Halloween reading.
A detective goes undercover as her double in Tana French's tense Dublin mystery; readers accept the silly premise.

books.t: The Spy Who Came in from the Cold
books.why: Le Carré's classic Cold War spy novel; readers praise its stunning twist.

books.t: Down and Out in Paris and London
books.why: Orwell's account of living in poverty in two cities; excellent, essay-like nonfiction.

pl.t: Na dnie w Paryżu i Londynie

books.why: The lives of three generations of Chinese women through the 20th century; recommended for its personal and historical sweep.
A girl travels across the US telling the story of her friend while dealing with her mother's absence; made one reader a reader.
Activist gardeners meet a billionaire in a thriller with unlikeable characters you cannot stop reading.
A prince with amnesia discovers he is royalty in a parallel world; a classic fantasy series.
A girl is swept into a magical archipelago in Barker's illustrated young-adult fantasy trilogy.
A man and his cat travel Japan visiting old friends; a gentle, tearful story readers recommend.
Asimov's novel about a parallel universe's energy source and truly alien aliens; readers like its originality.
Tayari Jones's story of two women from Louisiana looking for belonging and each other; readers love her work.
Sartre's novel of a man losing his grip on reality; readers say it unsettled them, a first existentialist read.
A girl is taken from a Mi'kmaq berry-picking family and raised elsewhere; readers say it is very good.
Bujold's first Vorkosigan novel, a romance between two officers from enemy worlds; the start of a loved series.
An obsessive friendship between two teenage boys turns dangerous; a Hitchcock-style LGBTQ+ thriller readers devour.
Pregnant teen girls in a 1970s home discover real witchcraft; a gripping, feminist horror read.
Humans are enslaved by an alien empire in the start of a new James S. A. Corey series; deserves more attention.
O'Neill's long investigation into the Manson murders and the official story; readers became obsessed with it.
Three sisters revive witchcraft in an alternate 1890s America; readers love the prose and feminist spirit.
A multigenerational Canadian family saga of secrets and tragedy; readers say its opening line stays with you.
A whimsical, magical story with inventive worldbuilding; one reader's only five-star book in nearly two years.
Krasznahorkai's long-sentence novel about a decaying Hungarian village and a charismatic con man; strange and demanding.
A boy falls into an underground world full of giant creatures; a good, underrated read for kids and parents.
A scandalous Gothic novel of a pious monk's downfall; readers found it lived up to expectations.
Camus's essay on absurdity and how to live well anyway; a reader says it helped them through hard times.
The fourth Dungeon Crawler Carl novel, a gruesomely funny survival-game adventure that fans of the series eagerly read.
Forster's short story of people living underground, entirely dependent on a machine; a prescient classic.
Eco's novel about editors who invent a conspiracy that comes true; spans two millennia of secret societies.
Rutherfurd takes you through three centuries of New York's history by following families; very long but enjoyable.
A boy in medieval England travels to Persia to learn medicine; readers say it is as good as The Pillars of the Earth.
A bookseller finds a book that can open doors anywhere; a fun fantasy suggested as a light read.

books.t: The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida
books.why: A dead photographer in the afterlife solves his own murder amid Sri Lanka's civil war; a Booker winner.
Linked creepypasta-style tales of childhood stalking; readers say it gave them chills.
Baldwin's novel of race, sexuality and friendship in 1950s New York; readers find it powerful and beautiful.
Gaddis's huge, difficult novel about art forgery and authenticity; admirers call it a masterpiece.
A wide-ranging space opera of wormhole travel and alien threat; readers like its scale though not all of its detail.
Two former friends become enemies with superpowers; recommended as a dark, fast take on the superhero story.
A knight seeks to restore a wizard-ruled realm in a book readers find unique and well-executed.
A girl must spin shirts of nettles to free her brothers in this Irish retelling of The Wild Swans; deeply loved.

books.t: All the ugly and wonderful things
books.why: A young girl and a much older man form a troubling bond; a difficult, uncomfortable book that stays with readers.
Allie Brosh's illustrated essays on depression and daily chaos, funny enough to cheer up a dying relative.
A farm girl becomes a soldier and paladin in a realistic fantasy series; a reader's most re-read book.
The 1854 London cholera outbreak and how a doctor and a priest traced it; a gripping blend of history and science.
Austen's novel of two sisters who find love and sense in Regency England; a recommended classic.
Lem's witty fables about two robot inventors; one reader says it is the hardest they have ever laughed.
Historians in WWII-era England cannot get home in this time-travel pair; readers say it is a favourite.
A doctor is drawn into a decaying country house haunted by something; a slow Gothic read for spooky season.
Ford's tale of two couples and an unreliable narrator; praised as a masterpiece of deception.
A food critic narrates how she kills her lovers and cooks them; graphic enough to warn people with weak stomachs.
Amis's brash, satirical novel of a debauched ad man in 1980s London; praised for its stylish prose.
A man involuntarily time travels and loves a woman across his jumps; a romantic favourite.
A thousand-page stream of thoughts of an Ohio housewife; readers find it hard going but admirably ambitious.
McKinley's gentle retelling of Beauty and the Beast; recommended as a cosy fairytale.
A wild wolf-dog's life in the Yukon and beyond; Jack London's classic of survival.
Banks's space opera of a slow-living alien species and a coming war; readers praise his writing.
A US marshal investigates a patient's disappearance from an island asylum; a one-sitting thriller.
Uris's saga of Ireland's struggle through the lives of Catholic and Protestant families; a favourite of historical epics.
King Lear on a farm in Iowa, showing a family tearing itself apart; praised and widely cited as a favourite.
A suburban couple's marriage crumbles in 1950s Connecticut; a bleak, powerful classic.
A burned man falls for a sculptor who claims to have known him in past lives; one reader's favourite.
Women in a Washington boarding house in the 1950s keep secrets; readers love Quinn's work.
A god narrates a story of a kingdom and its ruler; praised for its unusual narrator.
A near-future second American civil war seen through one girl's life; grim, gripping and widely recommended.
A young woman in Kentucky is drawn to a haunted house; enrapturing for readers who finished it in two days.
Selby's raw, shocking stories of Brooklyn's underworld; recommended as completely extreme.
Shakespeare's tragedy of the Danish prince and his revenge; the quintessential play.
Palahniuk's satirical novel narrated by the last member of a suicide cult; a reader found it gripping.
Erdrich's novel based on her grandfather fighting a 1950s bill to end Native tribes; vivid characters and a Pulitzer winner.
Lynda Barry's illustrated novel is a dark, shocking story of a girl on the run; readers call it utterly wild.
A young journalist's rare autoimmune disease nearly destroys her mind; a gripping medical memoir.
The second Red Rising book escalates the war between castes; a favourite of action-lovers.
A boy becomes obsessed with a possessed 1958 Plymouth; one reader's favourite King.
An alternate-history space race in the 1950s after a meteor strike, with a female mathematician at the centre.

books.t: The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat
books.why: Sacks's case histories of patients with strange neurological conditions; readers call it fascinating.

pl.t: Mężczyzna, który pomylił żonę z kapeluszem

books.why: A Danish girl helps her Jewish friend escape the Nazis in 1943; a school favourite readers think about for years.
Clarke's far-future tale of a perfect city and a young man who wants to leave it; a classic of old science fiction.
A retired man's memory of his youth is overturned by a late discovery; a short novel readers call mind-blowing.
Genetically engineered people who never sleep split society in this thoughtful near-future novel, with sequels.
O'Connor's Southern Gothic about a man founding a church without Christ; strange, dark and sharply comic.
Gogol's satire of a con man buying dead serfs; readers say it intrigues and entertains them.
A fictional take on the Ted Bundy crimes told from the women's side; a recommended true-crime-style thriller.

books.t: Snow Flower and the Secret Fan
books.why: Two girls in 19th-century China are bound as lifelong friends through a secret women's script; widely loved.
A comedy of manners in the Vorkosigan saga, mixing romance, politics and disaster dinners; a high point for fans.
Mary Karr's memoir of a chaotic Texas childhood with sharp humour; readers call it wonderful.
A winter-sleeping world is full of dreams and danger; very British humour that readers found damn funny.
A huge, wild novel about a ten-year-old self-proclaimed messiah at a Chicago school; ambitious and divisive.
Two gods give dogs human intelligence and watch what happens; readers call it a unique, moving fable.
A doctor learns of the Mayfair family of witches in a vast Gothic saga; a good pick for Anne Rice fans.
Pynchon's loosely plotted tale of a hippie-era family in California under Reagan; suggested as an easier way into him.
The US ambassador and his family in 1930s Berlin as Hitler rises; Larson's story reads like a thriller.

books.t: The Conspiracy Against the Human Race
books.why: Ligotti's bleak philosophical case that consciousness is a curse; for readers who like their pessimism uncompromising.
An Indian-American family across generations deals with names, tradition and loss; a quietly affecting novel.

books.t: The Girl Who Drank the Moon
books.why: A good witch accidentally gives a baby magic; a fairytale a child asked a parent to read.
A professor and his estranged mother's past connect in a funny, sprawling novel that readers couldn't put down.
An injured man paints terrifying things in a Florida island house; a King favourite, also great on audiobook.
Nabokov's gentle, comic story of a Russian professor at an American college; readers return to it.

books.t: Vera Wong's Unsolicited Advice for Murderers
books.why: A busybody tea shop owner turns detective when a body appears in her shop; a lighthearted cosy mystery.
A young killer is trained at a convent of fighting nuns in a gritty world; a memorable opening line.

books.t: The Girl Who Loved Tom Gordon
books.why: A nine-year-old lost in the woods clings to baseball; a short King that readers say hooked them on his work.
A female pilot's life and the actress who plays her decades later are intertwined; the story stayed with readers.

books.t: The Southern Book Club's Guide to Slaying Vampires
books.why: Women in a book club in South Carolina discover a vampire next door; a fun, gory horror comedy.
A tea monk and a robot talk about what people need; a short, comforting book called one of the best.

books.t: Illusions: The Adventures of a Reluctant Messiah
books.why: A pilot meets a messiah who teaches simple, hopeful lessons; readers re-read it as a comforting guide.
A babysitter finds disturbing drawings by her charge; a quick ghost story and thriller.
Two friends invent a magical kingdom in the woods and then face loss; a favourite childhood tearjerker.
A retired pirate captain takes one last job in the medieval Indian Ocean; praised as a lively pirate adventure.
The Dust Bowl told through the people who stayed on the Plains; recommended for fans of narrative history.
A mercenary seeks bloody revenge in Abercrombie's grim fantasy; a fast standalone that readers love.
A girl disguises herself as a boy to join the army in a Discworld satire of war and gender.
Theodore Roosevelt's near-fatal expedition down an unmapped Amazon river; an epic, harrowing true story.
Two divers find a sunken U-boat off New Jersey and try to identify it; great for wreck-diving fans.
A woman recounts her life and a murder to police in a monologue; a short, tough King novel.
A software engineer's mind becomes a self-replicating space probe; a funny, popular first book in the Bobiverse series.
A literary agent and an editor keep meeting in a small town; an easy, enjoyable romance even for non-fans.
A young woman joins a tech giant that demands complete transparency; a gripping near-future cautionary tale.
A physicist and a medieval priest link across centuries around visiting aliens; a rarely mentioned, well-loved book.
A lonely farm couple in Iceland face a mystery with a twist that left readers stunned; hard to put down.
Vonnegut's short story of forced equality and handicaps; readers say it stays with them for decades.
A paladin and a perfume maker end up on the run in a funny, warm fantasy romance with a cult following.
Oates's multi-voiced novel with a menacing teacher; readers warn it contains difficult content.
Virgil's epic of Aeneas and the founding of Rome; readers suggest Fagles's translation.
A pilot, a boy and a pull of time across space; lyrical enough to win over readers who dislike science fiction.
Banks's Culture novel about a huge ancient artifact and a royal family's war; has a lot of what the poster wanted.
A French-German SS officer narrates his war in this huge, disturbing novel; recommended for non-horror readers who want shocks.
A short fairytale-like fantasy about two sisters and a willow tree; a read for one afternoon.
A true story of a museum feather heist and its fly-tying obsessive; reads like a caper.
A girl dreams of becoming a starfighter pilot; an energetic YA novel that readers say fits the brief.
Everyone receives a box showing the length of their life; a popular, moving what-if story.
A man wakes from a coma with psychic powers; readers say it hooked them without knowing anything about it.
A writer and her formidable housekeeper form a complex bond in Hungary; praised as a deep, moving translated novel.
A teenage boy investigates the assault on his mother on a North Dakota reservation; a gripping, powerful Erdrich novel.
Discworld novel where Death takes a holiday to live as a farmhand; funny, warm and surprisingly moving about mortality.
Near-future thriller about water wars in the American Southwest, praised for feeling uncomfortably plausible.
A lonely, socially awkward woman slowly opens up; readers find it funny, heartbreaking and a gradual reveal.
A family drama about addiction and loss that readers find devastating but powerful.
A short, genuinely creepy tale of a girl and her sinister other mother, scary even for adults.
A working-class sailor tries to become a writer; readers say it broke them and mirrors their own ambition.

books.t: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride
books.why: Latest in the Dungeon Crawler Carl LitRPG series; fans love the dark humour and relentless inventiveness.
Cutting-edge sci-fi with strange alien tech and body horror; readers call it wild, with strong prose.
The pop star tells her own story of fame and control; readers find it honest and heartbreaking.

books.t: From the Mixed-Up Files of Mrs. Basil E. Frankweiler
books.why: Two siblings run away to live in a New York museum and chase a mystery; a beloved children's classic.
First part of The Lord of the Rings, the foundational quest fantasy that readers return to again.
A woman's account of growing up in a polygamist Mormon family in Mexico; tragic and gripping.
A teenager gets letters teaching her the history of philosophy inside a mystery; an accessible entry to the subject.
Sanderson's debut about a fallen magical city and the people trapped in it; fans praise its imagery and plot.

books.t: The making of the atomic bomb
books.why: Comprehensive, award-winning history of how the bomb was built, from the physics to the people; readers find it gripping.
A soul reincarnated thousands of times tries to get life right while loving Death; funny and warm.
True story of a family with many schizophrenic sons, reading like a novel and tracing the history of the illness.
A boy and a runaway slave drift down the Mississippi in Twain's satire of American society.
Hard sci-fi about Earth's destruction by alien machines, called stunning by readers who rate it among the best apocalypse novels.

books.a: Charles R. Pellegrino and George Zebrowski
books.why: Hard sci-fi about a ruthless alien first strike, loved for its cold logic on first contact.
Shows with data how a world designed around men harms women; readers find it eye-opening and infuriating.
A starship that can't stop accelerating hurtles through cosmic time; a classic of hard sci-fi, though some find it heavy on physics.
A cadet at a Southern military academy confronts a secret society; praised for lyrical prose and powerful storytelling.

books.t: Stories of Your Life and Others
books.why: Ted Chiang's thoughtful, precise short stories, including the one behind the film Arrival, widely named among the best sf collections.
A writer learns someone is stealing a plot he took from a student; readers enjoy the twisty literary thriller.
A roguish space con man is recruited to catch other criminals; a light, fun classic though some find it dated.
A mecha reimagining of China's only empress, with a furious heroine; readers call it a fun sci-fi and fantasy blend.
A British consul drinks himself toward ruin on the Day of the Dead in Mexico; lush, demanding modernist prose.
The actor's stories and life lessons in a distinctive voice; readers like it, especially as an audiobook.
A woman finds a portal to a strange otherworld through a museum wall; creepy with dark humour.
A teenager in Glasgow falls for a boy from the rival religion; devastating and long remembered by readers.
Gifted children go undercover at a strange school to stop a villain; a clever adventure good for read-aloud.
A band of ageing mercenaries reunite for one last mission; fans compare it to a fun D&D campaign.
A widowed novelist is haunted at his lakeside house; a slow, emotional ghost story some call King's favourite.
A quirky road trip story described as funny, sentimental and addictive, with a Wes Anderson feel.
A brief Asimov story tracing humanity's question about entropy across eons; named a favourite short story by many.
Mafia-style clans fight over magical jade in an Asian-inspired city; a sweeping, rich family saga.

books.t: The moon is a harsh mistress
books.why: A lunar colony rebels against Earth with the help of a self-aware computer; a classic, though not all like it.
Sequel to The Will of the Many in a Roman-style magical world; fans find it gripping though some find the series overhyped.
An old woman with an ear trumpet stumbles into cults and apocalypse in a surreal, absurd romp.
Explains the strengths of introverts; readers say it helped them accept themselves.
A careful, vivid account of the school shooting and its investigation; hard material but compulsively readable.

books.t: The Crimson Petal and the White
books.why: A prostitute climbs through Victorian London in a lush, immersive novel; readers praise it but find it bleak.
Neighbourhood boys try to understand five sisters in 1970s suburbia; haunting and lyrical.
A journalist follows explorer Percy Fawcett's vanished search for a lost Amazon city; gripping adventure non-fiction.
A spirited American heiress's choices in Europe unfold in James's subtle prose; some find it improves as it goes.
Earth must do well in a galactic song contest to survive; a flamboyant, absurd Eurovision-style romp.
Closing volume of Stephenson's Baroque Cycle, a vast historical saga of science, money and intrigue in Newton's England.
A grim space-horror tale aboard a starship encountering something terrible; a favourite of readers who like dark sf.
A restless former basketball star abandons his family; praised for prose style though the main character is unlikable.
Tom Robbins' playful, eccentric novel about art, religion and a giant turkey-shaped camper.
Readers enjoy spending time in the head of a deranged, difficult narrator in this darkly comic novel.
A queer, brutal post-apocalyptic horror novel readers describe as dark and unflinching.
Dahl's classic about a boy facing child-hating witches; so gripping it turned some kids into readers.
Winton's bleak post-collapse Australian journey, compared to The Road in a Mad Max setting.
A girl's fortunes collapse at boarding school but her imagination keeps her going; a gentle children's classic.
Bret Easton Ellis' debut of bored, drugged Los Angeles youth; disturbing and cold, a cult favourite.
A governess in a Victorian household turns violent; readers call it unhinged, funny and gothic.
A hapless junior lecturer stumbles through academic life; praised as one of the funniest novels ever.
Five residential-school survivors try to rebuild their lives; readers find it heartbreaking and powerful.
A carer and a paralysed man fall in love; readers say it made them cry, though its themes are debated.
A teenager grieves her uncle lost to AIDS in the 1980s and forms an unexpected friendship; tender and moving.
Two Iranian women's friendship across decades of upheaval; readers name it a top favourite.
Gentle riverbank adventures of Mole, Rat, Badger and Toad; a cosy children's classic with warm humour.
First Gormenghast novel, set in a vast decaying castle with grotesque characters; rich, gothic and unlike other fantasy.
A Holocaust survivor and psychologist tells her story of survival and healing; readers find it powerful and uplifting.
A comatose Scottish man replays his violent past while imagining a hunt in Africa; harsh, dialect-heavy Welsh.
Bukowski's semi-autobiographical tale of a drunken, wisecracking postal worker; darkly funny and fast.
A grieving dowager sets out on a pilgrimage and finds a mystery; a Hugo-winning, warm and thoughtful fantasy.
A far-future space opera told by a fallen hero recalling his youth; readers praise its scale and prose.
Bazterrica's follow-up to Tender Is the Flesh, a bleak dystopia in a walled city; liked, though many prefer her first.
Orwell's first-hand account of fighting in the Spanish Civil War; compelling and less famous than his novels.
Four damaged people shelter in an Italian villa at the end of World War II; lyrical and slow-burning.
Spare, powerful short stories of ordinary people; the title story is often named among the best ever.
A girl sent to Hawaii's leper colony grows up there; immersive, well paced and moving.
Quiet, touching stories of people in a small Colorado town; praised for plain, beautiful prose.
A young writer's account of cancer and recovery; readers say it is fantastic and read it fast.
Austen's playful satire of Gothic novels, following a girl who imagines horrors at an old abbey.
Challenges the standard story of early human society with new evidence; readers say it changed how they see history.
A mysterious shop sets neighbours against each other in a Maine town; readers say it kept them engaged throughout.
Sweeping novel of the founding of Israel after World War II; a school favourite that readers loved.
Dust Bowl Nebraska and a woman who stores others' memories; slow, beautifully written and a book-club hit.
A mother keeps reliving the day her son commits a murder; an inventive time-twisting thriller.
Two siblings discover a magical creature preserve; a popular children's fantasy series starter.
A soldier teams with the ghost of a traitor general in a calendar-based space war; dense but inventive.

books.t: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes
books.why: Prequel to The Hunger Games following the young future President Snow; fans of the series enjoy the backstory.
A Vietnamese grandmother and granddaughter live through war across generations; readers find it moving.

books.t: Alive: The Story of the Andes Survivors
books.why: True account of the rugby team who survived a plane crash in the Andes; absolutely gripping.
A human interpreter among aliens navigates politics and tea-drinking diplomacy; praised for superb alien worldbuilding.

books.t: Go Tell It on the Mountain
books.why: Baldwin's semi-autobiographical novel of a Harlem boy and his family's religious life; moving and rich in flashbacks.
Le Guin's experimental anthropology of a future people, mixing stories, poems and maps; a favourite of devoted readers.
A shy college girl slips into unreality in a haunting, psychological Shirley Jackson novel loved by her fans.
Young women compete on a reality-TV style compound; a sharp, unsettling debut that readers devoured.
A lunar reporter's life gets weird in Varley's witty future world; many readers call it a favourite of his.
Brunner's 1975 tale of a hacker on the run in a networked society, eerily close to the present.
A demon king wakes after years and untangles a political plot; praised though the cast and names take effort.
Two magicians revive English magic during the Napoleonic wars in a witty, footnoted alternate history.

books.t: Doppelganger: A Trip into the Mirror World
books.why: Klein explores how a mistaken identity illuminates conspiracy culture and today's politics; readers say it makes sense of the moment.
Michener's huge saga of one archaeological dig in Israel and the layers of history beneath it; a good thick read.
Machiavelli's guide on holding political power, famed for its cold realism; some find it dry.
A young writer's poverty and doomed love in 1930s Los Angeles; a raw, confessional voice.
Letters vanish from an island's alphabet in this epistolary novel; a quirky, witty and fast read.
A retired spy hunts a bioterrorist in a sprawling thriller; a long, fast and enjoyable page-turner.
A family gathers at an isolated house and begins dying; a twisty mystery readers call great.
An ageing painter revisits her childhood and a friend who bullied her; many name it their favourite Atwood.
Boys at an Irish boarding school, comic and tragic; readers call it genius and read it quickly despite its length.
A man is trapped in a sand pit with a woman; surreal, allegorical and unsettling.
A programmer takes up baking after a magical starter arrives; a quirky, light read.
A woman becomes obsessed with winning her perfect house in a cutthroat housing market; a gripping, fast thriller.

books.t: Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone
books.why: A mystery at a family reunion, in the style of Agatha Christie; recommended especially on audio.
A teenager goes silent after a traumatic event; a powerful, widely read school book that hit readers hard.

books.t: The Sailor Who Fell from Grace with the Sea
books.why: A widow's lover and her son's cruel gang in postwar Japan; short, chilling and elegant.
A survivor of the Andes plane crash tells it first-hand; readers find it fantastic and moving.
Ambrose's account of the Lewis and Clark expedition; readers rate the storytelling, though some find it heavy going.
A lifelike robot companion begins asserting herself in her owner's home; a thought-provoking, quick read.
Quiet, perfectly written stories of Indian and Indian-American lives; a Pulitzer-winning collection readers love.
A young heir uncovers a tangled Victorian inheritance mystery; tightly plotted with twists readers did not see coming.
An FBI profiler hunts a serial killer with help from Hannibal Lecter; a gripping thriller.

books.t: The Gate of the Feral Gods
books.why: Fourth book in the Dungeon Crawler Carl series, a violent, funny LitRPG that fans devour.
A magical-realist satire of a post-colonial African dictatorship; readers call it brilliant and funny.
A dolphin-crewed starship is stranded on a hostile planet in a space opera focused on adventure.
An elderly woman secretly kills people she thinks deserve it; funny, poignant and a bit disturbing.
A hundred tales told by young people sheltering from the plague, ranging from comic to tragic; a Renaissance classic.
Four-book saga of two friends from a poor Naples neighbourhood across a lifetime; readers reread it every few years.

books.t: The Worst Journey in the World
books.why: First-hand account of the Antarctic Terra Nova expedition and a brutal winter trek; a polar-exploration classic.
Journalist Keefe's reported narrative of a London story; readers called it outstanding.
Retells 1984 from the viewpoint of Julia, giving the regime's ideology and her experience more depth.
Fog-bound Scottish seaside horror with a gloomy atmosphere and a wild ride.
A commuter becomes entangled in a missing-woman case she glimpses from the train; a popular psychological thriller.
Grim rural Ohio and the violent people who live in it; brutal, gripping Southern gothic.
Sprawling cyberpunk saga of children trapped in a virtual world; fans say it ties together superbly.
Brunner's 1972 vision of ecological collapse told in fragments; readers say it grows more relevant each year.
An indigenous girl bonds with a dragon and goes to a colonial school; readers like its dragons and perspective.
Character-driven historical novel by the author of The Help; readers call it a long, page-turning story.
Schoolchildren are forced to fight to the death; a violent, gripping Japanese cult novel.
Second Vorkosigan novel following Cordelia after marriage into a military society; readers call the series awesome.
A woman lives happily in a haunted house, hiding the truth; beautifully written about marriage and survival.
First of the long Aubrey-Maturin series of Napoleonic naval adventures, rich in period detail.
A detective who believes everything is connected is drawn into a madcap mystery, as funny as Hitchhiker's Guide.
Reconstructs the loss of a fishing boat in a catastrophic 1991 storm; vivid and engrossing non-fiction.
A detective investigates a death among the giants in a wild sci-fi noir; delightful and inventive.
Whitman's landmark poetry collection celebrating the self and America; demanding but central to American literature.
Wilde's brilliant comedy of mistaken identities and Victorian manners, a favourite since school and university.
Saunders' sharp, inventive stories that readers say left their jaws hanging open.
The story of the clockmaker who solved the problem of finding longitude at sea; fantastic and compact.
A boy criminal mastermind kidnaps a fairy; loved even by reluctant readers.
A young mortician's memoir of working in a crematorium and facing death; funny and eye-opening.
A post-singularity adventure with action, twists and believable worldbuilding; readers think Williams is overlooked.
Stephen Fry retells the Greek myths with wit; especially enjoyed as an audiobook.
Corrie ten Boom's story of hiding Jews from the Nazis; very powerful and faith-driven.
A boy learns he is an agent of the Light in a classic children's fantasy about Light versus Dark.
Letters between a New York writer and a London bookseller grow from business to friendship; short and charming.
Linked short stories of lonely people in a small Ohio town; a quiet American classic.
A fictional geisha recounts her rise in pre-war Kyoto; a romantic, immersive read.
A hollow asteroid appears over Earth with a mysterious tunnel; hard sci-fi readers reread it often.
A whole novel of one man's lunch break, obsessing over small things; plotless but fascinating.
Interlinked lives of twelve mostly Black British women told in a fluid, punctuation-light style; readers reread it.
Three women break codes at Bletchley Park during World War II; a gripping, popular historical novel.
Asimov's classic title story, where a world of constant daylight faces darkness, plus other tales; relatable and gripping.
Dungeon Crawler Carl book 4; fans love its dark humour and relentless action.
Larson tells the 1900 Galveston hurricane through those who lived it; compelling and well researched.
A whale biologist hunts the secret of whale songs in a goofy Christopher Moore comedy.
A woman with unnamed mental illness navigates life; darkly funny and moving.
A mathematician helps a neighbour cover up a murder in a clever Japanese puzzle mystery.
Sequel to Gideon the Ninth with a puzzling, memory-fractured structure and morbid humour; best read after book one.
Pilgrims tell bawdy, moving and comic stories on the road to Canterbury; poetry and prose from medieval England.
Finale of Abercrombie's First Law trilogy, a bleak, cynical and fast-moving grimdark conclusion.
A detective pairs with a robot to solve a murder in a crowded future city; a classic sci-fi mystery.
A couple's trip to a remote Scottish chapel turns dangerous; one reader stayed up all night finishing.
Middle volume of The Lord of the Rings, with war and journeys; readers reread it again and again.
A woman drives the Scottish highlands picking up hitchhikers for a sinister purpose; strange, chilling and far deeper than the film.
A miser's life is changed by an abandoned child; moving, though some find the prose demanding.
A girl endures abuse by her father in rural California; powerful but extremely disturbing.
A young woman is drawn into smugglers' crimes at a Cornish inn; a gothic adventure.

books.t: The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch
books.why: A mystery drug and a sinister tycoon blur reality in Philip K. Dick's disturbing classic.
A family unravels after the death of a favourite daughter; devastating and beautifully told.
A comfortable family is shattered by his daughter's act in the Vietnam era; harrowing American portrait.
Explores the hidden world of fungi and how they shape life; almost overwhelming in its wonder.
Divers train to mine asteroids in a man-against-nature space thriller; similar in feel to Andy Weir.
A British journalist, an American agent and a woman in 1950s Vietnam; a short, moving anti-war novel.

books.t: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
books.why: A shy teenager's letters about friendship, love and trauma; a coming-of-age favourite.
Wells' classic Martian invasion of England, readers' first adult sci-fi and still timeless and fun.
The prosecutor's account of the Manson murders and trial; a gripping true-crime classic.

books.t: The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao
books.why: A nerdy Dominican-American boy and his family under a curse and a dictator; brilliant, voice-driven and slang-rich.
A hunter of dangerous gods teams up with a girl and a child in a high fantasy world; readers had a book hangover.
Burroughs' darkly comic memoir of a bizarre childhood with his mother's psychiatrist's family.
Second book of the Kingkiller Chronicle; Kvothe's tale continues, though fans wait years for the finale.
The Red Hot Chili Peppers singer's brutally honest memoir of addiction and survival; strong on audio.
Clavell's sweeping tale of rival traders founding Hong Kong; a long, gripping adventure.
A girl's possession and the priests who fight it; readers call it superbly written and genuinely scary.
Reported story of families in a Mumbai slum; gorgeous writing that left readers traumatized.
Tom Robbins' wacky love story of an outlaw princess and a bomber; readers burst out laughing.
Two women's friendship from childhood to middle age in Judy Blume's adult novel.
Two teens face a dark fairy-tale forest; a gothic, atmospheric YA horror favourite.
Austen's quieter novel of a poor cousin raised in a rich house; divisive heroine but rewarding.
Dillard's observations of nature near her Virginia home; gorgeous, meditative writing that earned a Pulitzer.

books.t: The Book of the Unnamed Midwife
books.why: A midwife survives a plague that kills most women in a bleak post-apocalypse; readers reread it often.

books.t: Maybe You Should Talk to Someone
books.why: A therapist goes to therapy herself; readers find it funny, warm and keeps making them laugh.
An anxious executive's inner monologue from the author of Catch-22; divisive, sad and eye-opening.
A scholar rises in an intellectual order devoted to a game of ideas; demanding, richly philosophical.
Sanderson's ongoing epic series of huge books, praised for original worldbuilding and magic.
A Western about a town and its gunman showing how perspectives change over time.
Springsteen's memoir in literary prose; especially good as an audiobook he narrates himself.
A woman is stuck repeating the same day in this quiet, much-praised Danish series.
An aging rock star buys a ghost online; readers say it scared them badly.
Epic Australian family saga of love and a forbidden priest; readers call it a piece of art.
A girl becomes a dragon-slaying hero in a classic fantasy that turned many young readers into book lovers.
Roy's memoir about her mother and her own path; readers who liked The God of Small Things find it incredible.
Story of the 1936 US Olympic rowing team told with narrative drive; a popular inspirational read.
A time-travel novel with paradoxes galore; some readers call it Asimov's best.
A background actor dreams of being the lead in the script of a cop show; formatted as a screenplay and sharply funny.
A hidden magical world woven into a carpet is hunted; readers find it mind-bending dark fantasy.
A farm boy is drafted into an absurd space war in this antiwar parody of military sf.
A reluctant college English department head faces a crisis in this campus comedy; readers say it is the funniest book they've read.
Gibson's story of a woman who finds a link to a future London; fantastic but telegraphic and demanding.
A town sealed between a valley of the past and the future; readers call it the best they've read.
Olympic figure skating partners fall into love and scandal, told like a documentary; compelling and dramatic.
Unfinished novel about boredom at an IRS center; hard and frustrating, but admired by DFW fans.
Hard sci-fi in the Xeelee universe with huge ideas and immense time spans.

books.t: The Heart is a Lonely Hunter
books.why: Lonely misfits in a Southern town gather around a deaf man; a moving American classic.
Wolfe's vivid account of the Mercury astronauts and test pilots; an all-time great of narrative non-fiction.
A six-part Southern gothic saga of a river family and its mysterious matriarch; fantastic and bingeable.
Alderman imagines tech billionaires and the end of the world; readers are sucked in and want to reread it.

books.t: The Book of Form and Emptiness
books.why: A boy hears objects speak after his father dies, and finds help in a library; tender and imaginative.
Kaysen's short memoir of her time in a psychiatric hospital in the 1960s.
A sick mother searches for who killed her daughter; the ending reveals how good it is.
Playful surreal stories narrated by a shape-shifting being across cosmic history; lovely and inventive.
A Zulu pastor searches for his son in Johannesburg during apartheid; moving and lyrical.
A noir detective romp in a strange future city that turns deeper; readers beg others to find it.
Imagined life of Jesus' wife, an independent woman in ancient Galilee; readers like its feminist take.
A neuroscientist reckons with family addiction and faith; readers were in shambles afterwards.
A fast, twist-filled thriller; readers call it bonkers and addictive, though some found it too long.
An old woman finds a note about a murdered girl and her imagination takes over; unsettling Moshfegh.
A poor young man's ambition leads to murder and trial; long but easy to follow.
Classic quest fantasy that got many readers started on the genre.
A video store clerk is drawn to a strange hole in the floor in this bleak cult horror.
The extraordinarily well-told story of the Chernobyl disaster and its causes.
A mathematician speaks with her psychiatrist in dialogue form; brilliant, smart and dense.
An orphan finds a hidden cottage to make her own; whimsical and wonderful.
A family prepares for the end of the world in a big house; an extremely mean Shirley Jackson novel.

books.t: The True Confessions of Charlotte Doyle
books.why: A girl sails on a ship with a mutinous crew; a children's favourite.
A standalone Cosmere romance between a girl and an artist who paint in dreams; easy and captivating.
Tiptree's collected stories, intense and moving; best taken in small doses.
A woman in Puritan Boston bears a mark of shame; a tough but rewarding school classic.
The Artful Dodger as an adult in a Dickens-flavoured adventure; familiar and fun.
Aliens save humanity after nuclear war at a cost; a master class in human motivation.
Philip Marlowe takes a case among gangsters and corrupt cops; the classic hard-boiled mystery.
Second Children of Time book, following strange non-human life forms; readers enjoy its alien biology.
An EMP attack shuts down America and a man protects his family; a top pick for readers of apocalypse fiction.
An old church deacon shoots a drug dealer in 1969 Brooklyn and the neighbourhood reacts; funny and warm.
A bullied boy befriends a strange girl in a Swedish suburb; a chilling vampire novel.
Two California families reenact Cain and Abel across generations; many readers call it phenomenal.
A senior demon coaches his nephew on tempting a man; witty Christian reflections on morality.
Twenty short lessons from history on resisting authoritarianism; a quick read.
A doctor arrives in a frozen medieval-style land with a strange parasite; brilliant body horror with mind games.
A teacher at a magical school faces a dark threat; readers call it absolutely brilliant.
A brand consultant tracks the maker of mysterious online footage; readers say it deserves the hype of Neuromancer.

books.t: The Word for World Is Forest
books.why: Humans colonise a forest world and its people resist; Le Guin's explicit commentary on the Vietnam war.
The final voyage of Captain Cook, beautifully told by Sides.
A square explores dimensions in a Victorian satire; loved for its formatting and ideas.
Follows eight families facing eviction and housing insecurity; eye-opening social research.
A young dragon and his friends search for a hidden valley; a children's favourite.
A haunted forest in a surreal alternate world; beautifully written and opaque, making readers ask what they are reading.
Teenagers try to prove meaning exists by sacrificing things; unsettling and philosophical.
Robots in a post-human world struggle to survive; readers like it for its AI characters.
A conservator traces the history of a rare Hebrew manuscript across centuries; readers enjoyed it.

books.t: I'll Be Gone in the Dark
books.why: A writer's obsessive hunt for the Golden State Killer, completed after her death; chilling and absorbing.
Alternate-WWI steampunk adventure with fabricated beasts and walkers; a series readers reread.
Personal essays about living with schizoaffective disorder, sharp and honest.
A group of friends in Monterey enjoy a ramshackle life; a funny, warm Steinbeck favourite.
Two rival Victorian magicians feud and sabotage each other; twisty, better than the film according to readers.
Adams and a zoologist travel the world to find endangered animals; a fun, witty book.
Two thieves become entangled in a kingdom's secrets in this fun, fast fantasy series.
A fugitive on an island sees mysterious people who may not be real; praised by Borges as nearly perfect.
A scientist makes a creature and rejects it; the Gothic classic about ambition and responsibility.
A girl in a failing alligator park in the Everglades goes on a surreal journey; haunting and unsettling.
A sensible young woman tidies a gloomy farm of relatives; riotously funny and reread annually by fans.
Four men on a canoe trip in Georgia face violence; short, intense and different from the film.
A naval officer's family faces the road to World War II; a long saga that readers call a favourite.
Women spies in World War I and a search in 1947; a popular historical page-turner.
Argues that crises are exploited to push free-market policy; a book some say they could not put down.
A young girl emerges from a fallout shelter after nuclear war; a childhood favourite.
A thief in a city where objects can be programmed with magic; inventive and fast-paced.
The assassination of President Garfield told as a compelling narrative; a one-sitting read.
Vonnegut's weird tale of a giant-sized future; hilarious and sad together.

books.t: The Girl with All the Gifts
books.why: A strange girl in a post-apocalyptic military base; tense, with a clever twist on the zombie story.
A girl travels with a white bear in a retelling of East of the Sun, West of the Moon; many reread yearly.
Final book of His Dark Materials, resolving the multiverse story; a genuinely satisfying conclusion.
A retired theatre director retires to the sea and becomes obsessed with a past love; readers rate it highly.
A musician's childhood in a cult and in poverty; dark and painful but powerful.
Based on the real Tennessee Children's Home Society scandal; readers cried and were broken-hearted.
A noblewoman hunts relics in a dying star system; a dark, sprawling space adventure with fantasy flavour.
Orwell's chilling vision of a totalitarian state and surveillance; its opening draws readers in.
Scottish heroin users in Edinburgh narrated in dialect; readers say it felt like a drug.
Castaways rebuild civilisation on a remote island in Verne's classic; loved since childhood.
Actor and producer Dunne recalls growing up among Hollywood stars and family tragedy; readers call it extremely cool.
A reporter discovers a lullaby that kills; a strange, darkly funny Palahniuk novel.
An immersive Old West tale of pursuit; readers call it so good they cannot recommend it enough.
A teen girl wakes in the afterlife and learns to live backward in age; a gentle, lasting story about death.
A Ponzi scheme and a remote hotel connect lives in Mandel's quietly eerie novel.

books.t: Deadhouse Gates (The Malazan Book of the Fallen, Book 2)
books.why: Second Malazan novel with a heartbreaking ending; readers want to walk the Chain of Dogs again.
Follows several families through two thousand years of London's history.
Argues that mass incarceration works as a racial caste system; eye-opening and widely recommended.
Medieval romance about Katherine Swynford and John of Gaunt; top-tier historical fiction some reread yearly.
A darkly comic LitRPG sequel where survivors fight through a deadly game dungeon; readers get hooked on the humour and relentless pace.
A retired detective hunts a killer who drove a car into a crowd; a gripping cat-and-mouse thriller that is easy to devour.
A boy's memoir of raising a pet raccoon in rural Wisconsin; a gentle, nostalgic story readers remember from childhood.
A near-future dystopia in which dreams are scanned for crimes, showing technology's grip on one woman's life; readers highly recommend it.
A young Ojibwe woman is pulled into a drug investigation in her community; a gripping thriller that adults enjoy too.
Wilkie Collins narrates Dickens's last years and a sinister mystery in Victorian London; a huge, immersive book that divides readers.
The Napoleonic Wars with an aerial dragon corps; a naval officer and his dragon make a charming, adventurous pair.

books.t: The Sound of a Wild Snail Eating
books.why: A bedridden woman observes a wild snail and finds meaning in slowness; readers facing illness find it quietly comforting.
A soldier's obsessive path through the English Civil War; praised as an unsettling, little-known gem.

books.t: Fried Green Tomatoes at the Whistle Stop Cafe
books.why: Warm Southern storytelling across generations built around women's friendship; recommended when friendship matters more than romance.
Two couples' friendship over decades told in quiet, beautiful prose; loved as a reflective, wholesome favourite.
A Japanese mystery solved through odd drawings and diagrams; a quick, addictive read that readers could not put down.

books.t: The Unselected Journals of Emma M. Lion
books.why: A light, witty 1880s journal-style story with a plucky heroine; recommended as comfort reading.
A young woman navigates Manhattan society in 1938; readers enjoy the elegant prose and period charm.
A professor faces early-onset Alzheimer's; readers find it heartbreaking and eye-opening.
A boy crosses into a mythic world and becomes a knight; a dense, unreliably narrated epic for patient fantasy readers.
A young writer befriends a Holocaust survivor in Brooklyn; readers call it devastating and unforgettable.
A surreal Glasgow epic mixing realistic youth with fantasy; recommended as one of the weirdest, most inventive novels.
Funny autobiographical essays about family and odd jobs; readers say it made them laugh to tears.
A short story about a high-tech nursery that turns sinister; readers say it stays with them long after.
A woman handcuffed to a bed in an isolated house; a harrowing, nerve-wracking survival story that readers find unforgettable.

books.t: Ducks: Two Years in the Oil Sands
books.why: A cartoonist's memoir of working in Alberta's oil fields; praised as a moving, honest account of isolation and harassment.
A librarian dreams of a lost city and finally travels there; a lushly written fantasy suited to teens and adults.
A Tennessee farm wife encounters a strange monarch butterfly migration and a clash over climate change; thoughtful and moving.
A stoner detective in 1970 Los Angeles chases a tangled case; Pynchon's most approachable and comic novel.
A dreamlike, hard-to-summarise tale of a strange commune; recommended as one of the weirdest and most beautiful short books.
A girl rises to become a mistress of Charles II's court; a long, gossipy, very readable saga.
A man confesses his sexual obsessions and smothering family to a therapist; a raucous comic monologue that divides readers.
A witty urban fantasy about a modern druid and his wolfhound; readers rewatch it and praise the audiobook narration.
A time-travelling scholar is stranded in Regency London among sorcerers; an inventive, twisty adventure with a satisfying ending.
A woman with an eating disorder becomes obsessed with a Jewish shop clerk; strange, funny and compelling.
A short essay on gift economies and abundance seen through a berry bush; readers keep recommending it.
Humanity's last pyramid refuge under a dead sun; a demanding, archaic-voiced classic that readers find rewarding.
A raw, sexually explicit portrait of bohemian Paris; readers find it lusty and defiant.
A boy's cotton-farm summer in 1950s Arkansas; a gentle non-legal Grisham that readers rate among his best.

books.t: I'm Starting to Worry About This Black Box of Doom
books.why: A comic horror-tinged adventure; readers say it made them laugh out loud more than almost any book.
Swarming nanorobots escape from a lab; a quick, gripping techno-thriller.
In a dystopian future, Indigenous people are hunted for their bone marrow; a short, moving book often assigned in school.

books.t: Just One Damn Thing After Another
books.why: Historians time-travel into disasters in a chaotic British institute; a witty, addictive series recommended for light reading.

pl.t: Just One Damned Thing After Another

books.why: A student writes a novel whose characters rebel against him; wildly funny Irish metafiction.
A woman fleeing a violent past reckons with men and rage; liked for its voice and unhinged intensity.
Stories behind the periodic table's elements and the people who found them; readers call it enthralling, not pedantic.
Short imagined dreams about different ways time might work; readers revisit favourite chapters.
A war veteran quits comfort to seek spiritual meaning; praised for Maugham's witty, observant take on people.
Discworld witches shake up a kingdom in a Macbeth parody; a funny, easy entry in the series.
A young Englishman comes to terms with loving men; a tender novel with a hopeful ending that readers reread.

books.t: The Five People You Meet in Heaven
books.why: A man learns the meaning of his life from five people in the afterlife; a short tearjerker.
A season as a park ranger in Arches National Park; funny, vivid nature writing with a sharp critique of modern life.
An astronaut wanders a hostile alien labyrinth alone; a short, claustrophobic and surprisingly fun novella.
Short vignettes of a Latina girl growing up in Chicago; a school favourite readers found good.
A teen convicted of killing a baby fights to prove her story; a twisty YA thriller with an unreliable narrator.
An online game ransomware scheme explodes into a global chase; a very long but breezy techno-thriller.
Two medieval friends, a monk and a wanderer, pursue opposite paths of spirit and sensuality; a beautifully written classic.
A young single mother turns to OnlyFans; funny and warm, and readers could not put it down.
An early plague apocalypse novel; slow in the first half but powerful and ahead of its time.
A sage and his strong-armed sidekick solve a mystery in mythical ancient China; hilarious, moving and often reread.
A girl meets a family who cannot die; a short, beautiful meditation on life and death.
A Civil War veteran secretly runs an alien transit station on his farm; a gentle Hugo winner readers love.
A woman caving on an alien planet depends on a handler with secret motives; a claustrophobic sci-fi horror.
Two powerful essays on race, religion and America; widely recommended as essential reading.

books.t: The Love Songs of W.E.B. Du Bois
books.why: A Black woman traces her family's history across generations of the American South; praised for beautiful writing.
A boy in Nazi-occupied Greece unwittingly helps betray his neighbours; a tearjerker readers recommend.
A drive around small-town America on back roads; a travel classic with descriptive prose.
Translators and identity in the Imperial Radch universe; readers enjoyed it, though earlier books help.
Hemingway's memories of young writing life in 1920s Paris; admired for its simple, beautiful language.
Fourth Red Rising book of relentless space war and politics; readers find it impossible to put down.
A pig is saved by a spider's words; a children's classic readers remember for its famous opening line and gentle wisdom.
Quirky, surreal sketches of America built around trout fishing; loved for its odd, memorable lines.
A Scottish family saga and mystery that opens with a famously striking first line; readers cherish Banks's mix of humour and darkness.
A federal agent wakes in a strange idyllic town he cannot leave; a gripping mystery with a big reveal, though a few readers disliked it.
Interlinked stories about a device that uploads memory; inventive and sharp, praised as stunningly good.
A charming con man slides into murder and identity theft in Italy; a suspense classic recommended for its chilling protagonist.
Commander Vimes confronts a dwarf-troll tension in Ankh-Morpork; a fan-favourite Discworld Watch story.
A man wakes with horns and the power to hear people's sins while hunting his girlfriend's killer; readers say it beats the film.

books.t: The Border Trilogy (All the Pretty Horses / The Crossing / Cities of the Plain)
books.why: Cormac McCarthy's three linked novels of cowboys in the borderlands; a recommended masterpiece for fans of Western epics.
Denis Johnson's raw debut about drifters on a doomed road trip; readers say it stuck with them.
A thief crew plots to topple an immortal ruler in a world of ash; a gripping, hard-to-put-down start to Mistborn.
The oldest man alive reflects on his many lives; readers say it changed their sense of what matters.
An orphan falls among London thieves; Dickens's classic about poverty and kindness, liked by readers who enjoy his style.
A poet's memoir about living with her eccentric Catholic priest father; praised as hilarious and beautifully written.
Two dogs escape a laboratory and struggle to survive; an uncomfortable but gripping story that readers say is well worth it.
A true-crime writer reconstructs a teen murder through interviews; compelling and addictive, with sharp 2000s culture.
A woman housed in a starship's shell works as its brain; a classic about humanity and technology.
A woman who gathers knowledge uncovers a mystery in a world that hides science; an underrated science-fantasy gem.
A young woman in a New England village falls into a doomed romance; praised as piercing and beautiful.
A huge space opera in which the dead return; a sprawling beast of a story some call so bad it is good.
Prisoners of war struggle to survive in a Japanese camp; recommended as gripping.
Humans and alien species fight cosmic threats in a Mass Effect-style space opera; good from start to finish.
Slasher survivors in therapy are hunted again; a clever, fast horror-comedy readers enjoy.
Neil Gaiman's dark fantasy comic about the lord of dreams; readers call it a masterpiece.
Disgraced spies exiled to a dead-end department stumble on a plot; sharp, witty spy fiction.
A girl runs away to a house of beekeeping sisters in 1960s South Carolina; a warm, popular coming-of-age story.
A girl guards her family against old spirits in medieval Russia; atmospheric folklore fantasy.
A grieving student discovers a secret society descended from Arthurian knights; an absorbing YA fantasy.
The sinking of the Lusitania told like a thriller; readers enjoy the fascinating detail.
A space opera of long journeys and slow time; liked for feeling fresh.
Beowulf's monster narrates his own story; readers reread it for its sublime prose.
A decent man in a small town is tempted into compromising his morals; a late Steinbeck about ambition and integrity.
Ankh-Morpork nearly goes to war over a rising island; a sharp, funny Watch story suggested to new readers.
A man recovering from an attack finds a skull in his family garden; twisty, though a few readers found it slow.
The prequel to Trainspotting follows how its characters fall into heroin; raw, intense and beautifully written.
A kitchen boy is swept into a kingdom's collapse; a classic epic fantasy that inspired many later writers.
Poe's famous poem of a grieving man and a croaking bird; short, dark and carefully constructed.
Children watch their adults squander a climate crisis and pandemic; a sharp, thoughtful novel, whatever the title suggests.
Life in a declining Maine town; Russo's Pulitzer winner mixes warmth and wry observation.
An elderly woman looks back on her life and family; comforting and richly descriptive.
A teenage girl with anxiety follows a missing-billionaire mystery; a warm YA about mental illness.
A paranoid thriller about a secret alternate-reality game; ridiculous and confounding in ways its fans love.
A Carmilla retelling in which a vampire helps a woman escape an abusive marriage; sensual gothic horror.
A foundling's bawdy adventures told by an ironic narrator; a delight for some, unreadable for others.
A boy grows up in a 1960s commune; called painfully beautiful, a contemporary Middlemarch.
The Challenger disaster told in gripping detail; readers recommend it alongside other strong narrative non-fiction.
Napoleonic Russia seen through several families; a monumental novel that readers tackle slowly.
A woman moves to a small town where witchcraft is afoot; a cosy, funny horror readers reread.
The Belgian king's brutal rule of the Congo; readers recommend it, though it is hard to take in.
A widow and a cursed swordsman bound to her sword make a warm, funny fantasy romance.

books.t: The Book of Strange New Things
books.why: A missionary travels to an alien planet while his marriage strains on Earth; weird, moving and praised for its ending.
Bryson tours the rooms of a house, revealing the history of everyday life; readers call it fun and fascinating.
Tommy Orange follows the descendants of a massacre survivor; readers find it amazing.
A darkly funny near-future satire about extinction credits; admired for its ideas.
A woman is repeatedly saved by a mysterious stranger tied to time travel; readers rank it his best.
A professor in crisis writes unsent letters to everyone; a brilliant, demanding portrait of a failed genius.

books.t: The Grace of Kings (The Dandelion Dynasty)
books.why: Two rebels topple an empire in a silkpunk world; well rated, though some find the pacing heavy.
A frank memoir of young adult depression; not for everyone but helpful for readers who relate.
The final Mistborn book, bringing the trilogy to a satisfying, epic close.

books.t: Stars in my pocket like grains of sand
books.why: Delany's galactic love story across cultures and unusual sexuality; difficult but rewarding.

books.t: Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said
books.why: A TV star wakes in a world where he does not exist; a paranoid Dick classic.
A clone raised in a drug lord's household fights to be treated as human; a school favourite people remember.
A Chinese couple separated by war across decades; recommended to fans of Pachinko.
A man hunts a killer across a ruined future city and through a strange past; dark, rich space opera readers praise.
A teenage girl speaks up after a police shooting of her friend; a moving YA that changed readers' views.

pl.t: The Hate U Give. Nienawiść, którą dajesz

books.why: A cosmic-horror novel about despair and obsession; readers call it the bleakest book they know, yet brilliant.
A minute-by-minute account of how a nuclear war would unfold; fascinating and terrifying.
A engineer defends genetically engineered workers fighting for freedom; a standalone Vorkosigan-universe novel, though not the best starting point.
A teen rides an elevator down while deciding whether to avenge his brother; a quick novel in verse praised for its form.
Eight generations of one Georgian family across the twentieth century; a huge book readers could not stop reading.
Two Jewish boys in 1940s Brooklyn form an unlikely friendship; an all-time favourite for many.
A hard-science sequel to Blindsight about post-human minds; hugely ambitious, though some readers cannot engage.
Three metaphysical detective stories in New York; readers find it weird and unforgettable.
The rise of forensic science through Jazz Age poison cases; engrossing history and chemistry.
An American couple unravels in the Sahara; a dark, haunting classic.
A Victorian visionary fantasy about a library and a dreamlike other world; admired by C. S. Lewis.
A girl befriends a gentle giant who blows dreams; a beloved Roald Dahl favourite.
A dark retelling of the Donkeyskin fairy tale about surviving abuse; strong but with serious content warnings.

books.t: Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee
books.why: The destruction of Native American nations told from their side; recommended as history that brings the past to life.
King Lear retold through the court jester with plenty of bawdy jokes; readers rank it near Lamb.
A desperate man joins a lethal TV game show in a dystopian future; a quick, punchy Bachman novel.

books.t: The Restaurant at the End of the Universe
books.why: The second Hitchhiker's Guide book sends its heroes further across a ridiculous galaxy.
A strange modernist novel about love and ruin among Paris expatriates; confounding but rewarding.
A Syrian-American man trapped in New Orleans after Katrina; a gripping true story readers recommend.
A man's search for spiritual enlightenment in ancient India; a short book readers return to.

books.t: The Absolutely True Diary of a Part-Time Indian
books.why: A boy leaves his reservation school for a white high school; funny and honest.
Three men keep a stash of cash and spiral into paranoia; so intense readers need breaks.
A competitive swimmer's obsession turns into body horror; best read as literary fiction.

books.t: The Cloud Roads (Books of the Raksura)
books.why: Shapeshifting winged people and a lost outcast in a rich fantasy world; recommended for fresh worldbuilding.
Kids in 1960 small-town Illinois confront an ancient evil; nostalgic coming-of-age horror.
A theatre director in pain gets a strange bargain in a surreal, disorienting novel readers love for its weirdness.
A porn-star record attempt narrated by several voices; a wild ride for Palahniuk fans.
A disfigured genius haunts the Paris Opera; a gothic romance about unrequited love.
Four women's lives in a time of pandemic; chosen by a book club.
A novel supposedly written by an exiled Hitler; a clever and funny satire of fascist fantasy.
An aging painter recalls his life and art; one of Vonnegut's favourite late novels.
A detective investigates a cult leader's murder in a bizarre, brutal tale; weird and brilliant.

books.t: The Last Murder at the End of the World
books.why: A murder mystery in the last human village; clever but divisive.
A family chases dreams across the American West; praised as a semi-autobiographical saga.
A serial killer's final hours told through the women around him; a top read for many.
A young man's ambitions rise and fall in post-Napoleonic France; a classic of ambition.
A princess runs off to be a dragon's helper; a witty fairy tale spoof.
Four King novellas including the basis for The Shawshank Redemption; readers love all of them.
A journalist digs into the death of a reclusive horror director's daughter; creepy and absorbing.
A heartbroken young woman finds comfort in her uncle's Tokyo secondhand bookshop; a short, gentle read.
A sexually transmitted dream city draws lost people; delightfully unhinged, Mieville-like.
A mystery and horror story solved through floor plans; so quick that readers finish it in one sitting.
A self-help book about letting others be themselves and focusing on yourself; readers say it shifted their perspective.
A world with no births awaits its final generation; a literary dystopia.
A society falls apart in a terrifying chase thriller; split opinions, but some read it in one sitting.
A stranded student finds a kidnapped child in a snowed-in rest stop; a fast thriller.
A Black single mother struggles against poverty in 1940s Harlem; recommended for its power.
A man wrongfully condemned spends 30 years on death row; a moving story of survival.
A short story about a human boy and an alien host; widely recommended for its unsettling beauty.
Knights, outlaws and rivalry in medieval England; an adventure classic with archaic language.
Digital afterlife and mind uploading played out over generations; ambitious but weaker than his best.
A grim, compelling story of a young man's life in jails and on the margins; one of the best ones for some readers.
Kerouac's story of mountains and Buddhism with Beat friends; good for self-discovery.
A woman on a strange trip heading towards a shocking end; short, odd and easy to read.
The sinking of the Edmund Fitzgerald on Lake Superior; recommended for its gripping detail.
A small English village erupts after a councillor dies; depressing but overlooked.
Tove Ditlevsen's three memoirs from childhood to addiction; stunning if not joyful.
Women fight for control of a living world-ship; imaginative and gnarly.
A talented baseball shortstop loses his confidence at a college; liked by many, though a few found it only so-so.
A copywriter in a corporate-ruled world is plunged into intrigue; a prescient dystopia.
A hunt for a man-eating tiger in the Russian Far East; far more than an animal story.
One man waging a guerrilla war on an enemy planet; darkly funny and clever.
Surreal, queer stories about women's bodies; recommended collection.
A young man is drawn into an aristocratic Catholic family; a wistful, elegant classic recommended for fans of dark academia.
Girls banished for a year to shed their supposed magic; a Handmaid's Tale-meets-Hunger Games YA, though one reader found it derivative.
Scientists try to decode a message from space and learn the limits of understanding; a philosophical Lem classic.
A crew races to harvest fuel from an exploding star in a Moby Dick-inspired space adventure; recommended classic sci-fi.
A Wall Street trader's life collapses after a hit-and-run in 1980s New York; a sharp satire that changed how readers saw the city.
A minister is sent to clear a remote Scottish island in the 1840s; a short, atmospheric and beautiful book.
Staff and guests at a Florida theme park build a society after a hurricane; told as interviews and compared to Lord of the Flies.
A soldier is given a gift of 250 horses in a Tang-inspired empire; a tragic and satisfying historical fantasy.

books.t: Things Have Gotten Worse Since We Last Spoke
books.why: A short, disturbing horror novella about two women's online relationship; readers are split but some insist you read it.
A young man trains for revenge in a society of dragon-riding fighters; a gripping, underrated military fantasy.
A dead programmer's software takes over the world; a techno-thriller with a sequel, recommended by tech-minded readers.
