A believable political thriller of how World War III could start; recommended for readers who like long, realistic thrillers.
Another Dungeon Crawler Carl installment; the series readers are addicted to for humour and gore.
A cyber-Frankenstein tale about an AI consciousness and a monster; a book club in which everyone loved it.
A device lets people view the past, with huge social consequences; readers remember its ideas decades later.
Banks's non-Culture novel set in a vast castle-like future, with a phonetically written narrator; clever and strange.
A fantasy-western revenge quest in the First Law world; gritty and violent, with Abercrombie's sharp wit.
A South American revolution and a silver mine told with beautiful, dense prose; a Conrad masterpiece for patient readers.
Old men haunted by a shared secret and a vengeful ghost; considered one of the scariest classic horrors.
Bukowski's alter ego grows up miserable in Depression-era Los Angeles; resonates with disenfranchised teens.
A pregnant woman suspects her neighbours' sinister intentions; a paranoid, quick classic horror.
A party travels the ruins of America centuries after a collapse; an overlooked post-apocalyptic adventure.
An argument that television turns public life into entertainment; readers say it still feels sharp.
A troubled Irish boy's voice narrates his descent into violence; harrowing and brilliant.
A novelist's short, honest account of his severe depression; heavy but excellent.

books.t: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader
books.why: A boy sails to the edge of the world with Narnia's heroes; famous for a memorable first line.
Funny, weird stories from a gas station night shift; the audiobook narrated by the author is particularly recommended.
A woman in Alaska becomes entangled with a stranger and the wild; beautiful prose and a bold story.
The Trojan War retold through the women who lived it; recommended for fans of Greek myth.
A genetically engineered fighting dog questions his orders; a fun, thoughtful military sci-fi, though one reader warns against it.
The first full-length Murderbot novel; a Nebula-winning sarcastic robot adventure.
A temp worker for supervillains plots revenge against a hero; a fun superhero satire more than sci-fi.

books.t: Mrs. Frisby and the Rats of Nimh
books.why: A field mouse seeks help from super-smart rats; a childhood classic that seems small but holds depth.
A shapeshifting alien learns to move in a human body; bodily horror and satire from Korea, an unhinged ride.
Two writers compete to tell a woman's life story; an Emily Henry romance, rated weak by some.
A hallucinatory satire of a world dosed with drugs; rapid-fire ideas readers adore.
Ta-Nehisi Coates's essays on storytelling, Senegal, Carolina and Palestine; readers call it a top nonfiction pick.
A man pieces together a lost childhood in a wandering, memory-driven narrative; loved for its amazing sentences.
A time-slip alternate-history love story with sea battles and mysterious letters; a rarely mentioned gem.
A husband wrongfully imprisoned returns to a changed marriage; praised for its emotion and complexity.
A young messenger rides with a dying courier's secret in a magical kingdom; solid series start with a heroine.
Two families of different classes intertwine in Edwardian England; a beautiful classic about connection.
The second Dungeon Crawler Carl novel, loved for its dark humour and addictive pace.
Four kids find a coin that grants half of each wish; an inventive classic for reading aloud.
The doomed Arctic voyage of the USS Jeannette told like a thriller; so unbelievable it reads like fantasy.
Explorers find a vast subterranean world beneath the earth; an all-time favourite for some, not for all tastes.
Steinbeck's linked stories of a boy and his horse on a California ranch; a quick read, but some find it slight.
An astronomer in the Arctic and an astronaut in space struggle with isolation after an apocalypse; a quiet, moving read.
An expedition to Halley's comet by two science fiction authors; a fondly remembered hard SF adventure.
A boy blinded in a shipwreck survives on an island with an old man; a school favourite that changed readers' lives.
A murder is planned in a world of telepaths; a Hugo-winning sci-fi classic recommended often.
A Marine's raw memoir of fighting in the Pacific in World War II; widely respected.
Four generations of a Palestinian family; readers say it left them sobbing.
Borges's imaginative short stories about infinity, libraries and mirrors; readers reread them many times.
A biologist reintroduces wolves to Scotland while hiding her own past; beautiful but depressing.
A film-noir mystery in an alternate solar system; weird, ornate, recommended to fans of Southern Reach.
An American writer's trip to Calcutta turns to nightmare; unsettling, tragic and not forgettable.
An investor's account of uncovering Russian fraud and the death of his lawyer; a gripping page-turner.
The first book of the Alexandria Quartet, a lush tale of love and intrigue in 1930s Egypt.
Two witch sisters grow up with a family curse; a warm, magical tale of sisterhood.
An occupied city with factions and a rebellion; praised for its characters, especially Ilmar.
Ken Kesey's Merry Pranksters travel across America in a bus; a fun, wild read for rock-history fans.
A strange boarding school for disabled teens with its own rules and myths; a wild and confusing ride that rewards patience.
A Pennsylvania neighbourhood's secrets over decades; recommended for book clubs and James McBride fans.
A huge free web serial about an inn in a fantasy world; readers call it absolutely amazing.
A man obsessed with football and the New York Giants unravels; readers call it hilarious and sad.
Two women centuries apart chase a chess set with secret powers; a real page-turner.
The second Discworld book continues the wizard Rincewind's misadventures; adored even though it is rarely praised.
Elephant-like aliens invade Earth in an engaging hard-SF clash; great alien-invasion fun.
Two women with shared birthdays and a podcast, with a plot twist readers loved.
Bukowski's alter ego drifts through dead-end jobs and bars; raw, coarse and short.
A very dark retelling of Alice in Wonderland with trafficking and violence; flagged for content warnings.
A leper is thrown into a fantasy world he refuses to believe in; an influential but heavy series.
How US-backed anti-communist killings in Indonesia shaped the Cold War; readers could not put it down.
The Greek queen's story from princess to vengeful ruler; a favourite mythic retelling.
A Black slaveowner in antebellum Virginia; a Pulitzer winner some call the best novel they have read.
Two families are blended and reshaped over decades; a warm, perceptive novel.
A dying clockmaker's last days and his father's memories; poetic Pulitzer winner.
Feist and Wurts's tale of political intrigue in a Tsurani-inspired empire; a standout in the Riftwar saga.
The Trojan War is replayed by gods on Mars, with robots and scholars; a perfect sci-fi and fantasy blend.
A woman with a magical garden and her sister in a small North Carolina town; sweet, easy and light.
A psychological thriller about a nurse at a prison; twisty page-turner fans.
A young lawyer discovers his firm's dark secrets; a classic legal thriller devoured on a single flight.
A model gets caught in a surreal terror plot in Ellis's satire of celebrity; wild and not for the faint of heart.
A year spent observing New York's rats; fascinating nature writing.
A spirited woman farmer attracts three suitors in rural England; turned one reader into a Hardy fan.
A woman befriends a blogger she admires and things turn unsettling; a good Japanese novel, though not as good as Butter.
A mute boy and his family's dogs, retold from Hamlet; readers say it made them bawl.
Two sisters, one suicidal; heartbreaking yet funny.
A servant narrates his rise from poverty in India through crime; a savage, funny class satire.
A Culture novel set in a medieval-style world; beautiful for some, a slog for others.
A girl travels north with an alethiometer and a daemon; the novel that turned a non-reader into a reader.
Four simple rules for personal freedom; short, clear and helpful for many readers.
The months between Lincoln's election and the Fort Sumter attack; compelling but long and slow for some.
A big biography of Ulysses S. Grant; absorbing despite the 1000-plus pages.
A young teacher goes to an Appalachian mission school in 1912; a beloved, inspiring read.
A farm couple faces a stranger offering to replace the husband; short, eerie and engaging.
A poet-linguist decodes an enemy language that shapes thought; a gem of classic sci-fi.
King's collection of short stories and novellas, including The Jaunt; varied and scary.
A New Jedi Order novel regarded as the series' peak and one of the best Star Wars books.
A fantasy-horror novel readers began and enjoyed; a new release with early positive buzz.
A cranky woman reinvents herself in a small town; warm and funny Backman.
Two teens in a gated Mexican community plan something terrible; short, wild and disturbing.
A cranky Montrealer's memoirs with a murder mystery; funny without trying to be.
Richard Wright's story of growing up Black in the Jim Crow South; a memoir that readers recall for its power.
A girl finds she is an elf with telepathic powers; a series fans love and read together.
A boy enters a school at the edge of a magical world; underrated and an all-time favourite for its fans.
Harpo Marx's life from vaudeville to Hollywood; a warm tale of a genius and a mensch.
Four women endure the siege of Masada; hauntingly beautiful.
The second MaddAddam book follows survivors of a plague and a religious sect; some like it better than the first.
Austen's epistolary novella about a manipulative widow; wicked and unlike her other books, though one reader disliked it.
A scholarly predator narrates his obsession; a beautifully written but disturbing classic.
A hard-SF adventure in the asteroid belt with a competent hero; devoted fans call it an addictive read.
An actor uncovers his abusive father's past and family secrets; stays with readers years later.

books.t: Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children
books.why: A boy discovers a hidden home for peculiar kids, told with vintage photographs; more horror than fantasy.
Phil Knight tells how he built Nike; so readable that non-readers finished it in a week.
An immortal official guides an alien tourist through a ruined Earth; a Zelazny classic with a mythic feel.
